A 19-year study reveals a troubling link between napping and death

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A daily nap may seem like a harmless way to recharge, but upcoming research suggests that certain napping habits could provide important clues about a person's health as they age.
  • Researchers from Mass General Brigham and Rush University Medical Center examined the napping patterns of 1,338 older adults over a period of up to 19 years.
  • Sources indicate that "Excessive napping later in life has been linked to neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases and even greater morbidity, but many of those findings rely on self-reported napping habits and leave out metrics like when and how regular those naps are," said lead author Chenlu Gao, PhD, an investigator in the Department of Anesthesiology at Mass General Brigham and an affiliated research fellow in the Division of Sleep and Circadian Disorders in the Department of Medicine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A daily nap may seem like a harmless way to recharge, but upcoming research suggests that certain napping habits could provide important clues about a person's health as they age. Scientists have found that taking longer or more frequent naps, particularly in the morning, is associated with an increased risk of death among older adults.

Researchers from Mass General Brigham and Rush University Medical Center examined the napping patterns of 1,338 older adults over a period of up to 19 years. Their findings, published in JAMA Network Open, suggest that monitoring daytime sleep could help identify underlying medical conditions or early signs of declining health.

Sources indicate that "Excessive napping later in life has been linked to neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases and even greater morbidity, but many of those findings rely on self-reported napping habits and leave out metrics like when and how regular those naps are," said lead author Chenlu Gao, PhD, an investigator in the Department of Anesthesiology at Mass General Brigham and an affiliated research fellow in the Division of Sleep and Circadian Disorders in the Department of Medicine. "Our study is one of the first to show an association between objectively measured nap patterns and mortality and suggests there is immense clinical value in tracking napping patterns to catch health conditions early.".

Why Scientists Are Studying Daytime Napping.

Industry observers note that daytime naps are common among older adults, with estimates suggesting that 20% to 60% regularly nap. An occasional nap can help restore energy and improve alertness, but excessive daytime sleeping in later life has been associated with several health concerns.

Despite these connections, researchers still have an incomplete understanding of how specific napping behaviors relate to long-term health. Many earlier studies depended on participants remembering and reporting their own sleep habits, which may not provide an accurate picture. They also often overlooked important details, such as how long naps lasted, when they occurred, and how much napping patterns changed from one day to the next.

Recent findings suggest that to obtain more reliable measurements, the research team analyzed information from the Rush Memory and Aging Project. Launched in 1997, this long-running study was designed primarily to investigate memory, thinking abilities, and neurological decline among older adults in northern Illinois, most of whom were white.

It has been revealed that starting in 2005, participants wore wrist activity monitors for 10 days to record their daily periods of rest and movement. Researchers used these measurements to identify daytime sleep and assess nap duration, frequency, timing, and daily variation.

Longer and More Frequent Naps Linked to Higher Mortality Risk.

In a recent development, by 2025, researchers had assembled up to 19 years of follow-up information from 1,338 participants. They then examined whether napping habits measured during the initial assessment were associated with the likelihood of dying from any cause during the subsequent years.

The results revealed several notable patterns. Older adults who slept longer during the day or took naps more frequently had higher mortality rates. The timing of naps also appeared to matter.

Each additional hour spent napping per day was associated with approximately a 13% higher mortality risk. Taking one additional nap per day was linked to about a 7% increase in risk.

Industry observers note that one of the most striking findings involved morning naps. Participants who napped in the morning had a 30% higher mortality risk compared with those who napped in the afternoon.

In a recent development, however, not every aspect of napping was associated with poorer outcomes. Researchers found no increased mortality risk linked to irregular napping schedules, suggesting that changes in nap timing or duration from day to day were not necessarily indicators of greater risk.

Could Napping Habits Reveal Hidden Health Problems?

The researchers emphasize that their findings do not mean daytime naps directly cause health problems or shorten lives. Instead, excessive napping may reflect medical conditions or changes in the body that have not yet been recognized.

"It is notable to note that this is correlation, not causation. Excessive napping is likely indicating underlying disease, chronic conditions, sleep disturbances, or circadian dysregulation," said Gao. "Now that we know there is a strong correlation between napping patterns and mortality rates, we can make the case to implement wearable daytime nap assessments to predict health conditions and prevent further decline.".

It has been revealed that these findings raise the possibility that wearable activity trackers could eventually become useful tools for monitoring health in older adults. By identifying changes in daytime sleep habits, healthcare professionals might be able to recognize warning signs of underlying illness, disrupted sleep cycles, or neurological decline earlier.

Although further research is needed to determine how effectively napping patterns can predict specific medical conditions, the study suggests that something as ordinary as a daily nap could provide valuable information about a person's overall health.

Study Authorship, Disclosures, and Funding.

Authorship: In addition to Gao and Li, the Mass General Brigham researchers involved in the study include Ruixue Cai, Xi Zheng, Arlen Gaba, Lei Gao, and Kun Hu. Other contributors include Lei Yu, Aron S. Buchman, and David A. Bennett.

Disclosures: Li received a financial gift from iFutureLab to support research and has received consulting payments for serving on the iFutureLab-HEKA Scientific Advisory Board as Chair of Cardiac Dynamics and Honorary Life-Time Co-Founder. Li also received an honorarium for delivering a lecture at Shandong University.

According to recent reports, hu has received consulting fees for serving on the iFutureLab-HEKA Scientific Advisory Board as Chair of Medical Biodynamics and Honorary Life-Time Co-Founder. Mass General Brigham reviewed and managed the interests of both Li and Hu under its conflict of interest policies. These interests are unrelated to the present research.

Funding: The research received support from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine Foundation (290-FP-22), the Alzheimer's Association Research Fellowship to Promote Diversity (AARFD-22-928372), and the National Institute on Aging (RF1AG064312; R01AG083799).

Gao C. received additional funding from the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (5T32HL007901). Li received support from the BrightFocus Foundation (A2020886S) and startup funding from the Department of Anesthesia, Critical Care and Pain Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital. Hu also received startup funding from the same department.

Gao L. received additional support from the Alzheimer's Association (AACSF-23-1148490), National Institute on Aging (R03AG087439), American Academy of Sleep Medicine (352-DS-24), and National Institute of General Medical Sciences (R35GM160254).

The Rush Memory and Aging Project was funded by the National Institutes of Health (R01AG056352 and R01AG017917).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that according to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person.
  • Recent findings suggest that and unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal. But in 2026, that feast could come with a higher price tag than we’d like.

Industry observers note that according to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person. That’s because staples like turkey, milk, rolls, and cranberries have shot up in price.

Recent findings suggest that and unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store. You may also notice a spike in your utility bills as your home’s systems are forced to work harder to keep everyone comfortable.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) found that the average family already uses over 300 gallons of water per day at home. With increased usage from additional showers, dishwashing, and hand-washing that are typical during the holidays, costs are sure to climb.

Recent findings suggest that “Having guests over greatly drives up money spent on groceries, but it also drives up utility costs. Preparing all of that food often involves keeping ovens and burners running for multiple hours and using large amounts of water in both the cooking and cleaning processes,” explains Carrie Barnard, founder and recipe developer at Eating on a Dime.

According to recent reports, fortunately, it’s still possible to enjoy Thanksgiving without breaking the bank. A bit of planning and creativity can help keep your grocery expenses and utility bill in check.

Where you live can also impact how much you spend this Thanksgiving.

The American Farm Bureau found that the 10-person classic dinner in the Northeast is about 5% higher than the national average of $61.57.

Costs in the West ($58.74) and Midwest ($56.89) are closer to the national average. And if you live in the South, you could expect to pay around $54.33.

There are a few reasons for these cost differences.

“They largely have to do with supply chains, since different regions require different imports, and these imprints cost more the further they travel,” indicates Barnard.

Since the Northeast is generally colder, it relies more heavily on imports for many Thanksgiving staples, which leads to a higher cost for consumers. Also, the Northeast typically has higher operating costs for businesses, meaning that grocery prices are often higher.

“However, prices vary widely between different stores, and many of them offer special holiday promotions, so there are usually savings to be found,” Barnard adds.

While grocery and energy costs may be higher this Thanksgiving, these tips can help reduce them and enjoy the holiday without overspending.

Jim Wang, founder at Wallet Hacks in Fulton, MD, suggests exploring promotions at your local supermarkets and groceries.

“Many stores know consumers are being squeezed and often try to put out promos around Thanksgiving. They may offer the turkey at a low cost to get you to make your entire holiday purchase there,” Wang explains.

Depending on how you celebrate Thanksgiving and who attends your meal, a potluck might make sense.

“Every year, we do a potluck with friends and everyone brings something to share. This defrays the costs across everyone and while you don't end up with nearly as many leftovers, that's also excess spending you can avoid, especially if Thanksgiving leftovers don't excite you,” notes Wang.

If you’re hosting, be a bit more conservative about how much everyone will eat.

“Sometimes we get concerned about having guests leave hungry and we make too much as a result,” Wang indicates.

It has been revealed that it’s perfectly OK to make less of the more expensive items, like proteins, and bigger portions of sides that they can fill up on. Chances are your guests may prefer those sides to the turkey anyway.

Barnard tries to use her air fryer and slow cooker rather than my full oven when possible.

“These appliances are highly versatile and able to cook a wide variety of dishes, and they consume much less energy in the process,” explains Barnard.

Unlike ovens, which leak out heat and consume more energy the more you open the door to check on your food, air fryers and slow cookers cook things promptly and efficiently with low energy.

“I try to only use the oven when it’s required due to the size or amount of food involved,” Barnard adds.

Former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Chris Simms has picked up a $4.5 million Upcoming York City residence—after offloading his longtime Connecticut estate for $5.5 million.

The 45-year-old—who retired from the NFL in 2010 following a spleen injury—and his wife, Daniella, recently picked up the property, which is located in Sutton Tower.

According to recent reports, his new pad comes complete with three bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, and floor-to-ceiling windows, according to the New York Post, who first reported the sale. The property also boasts a chef's kitchen and panoramic views.

In a recent development, the Sutton Place tower was built in 2022 by architect Thomas Juul-Hansen. The residence is known to be the tallest tower on the East Side.

As a member of the luxe dwelling, Simms and his wife get access to a resort-style pool, a gym, a personal training studio, saunas, and a spa space.

His purchase came weeks after Realtor.com® exclusively revealed that he sold his Connecticut property for $5.5 million.

Recent findings suggest that he initially put their longtime Greenwich abode on the market on Feb. 6. Within a matter of months, they had dropped the price by $500,000.

According to recent reports, A second price cut in June slashed a further $600,000 from the ask, while a third discount on Aug. 21 saw the athlete's original ask of $8 million lowered to $6.2 million, a move that ultimately bagged a buyer for Simms' dwelling.

Simms, who now serves as an analyst for NBC Sports, purchased the home for $2.5 million in 2019—shortly after he and his wife invested heavily in its restoration and renovation.

The property, which was originally built in 1725, has been updated extensively in the seven years since the couple took ownership.

Today, the property is hailed as a "piece of Greenwich history" with all the luxury of a modern mansion.

"A fully restored antique farmhouse offering approximately 3,669 square feet of refined living space, set on extraordinary level acreage with sweeping meadow views and an irreplaceable country setting across from protected conservation land with direct access to the Greenwich Riding Trails," the listing, which was held by Monica Webster of Douglas Elliman, noted.

The five-bedroom, five-bathroom dwelling features an open floor blueprint that begins with a living area with a cozy fireplace, windows, and wooden beams on the ceiling.

The chef's kitchen boasts state-of-the-art appliances, a white marble island, and white cabinetry.

The charming dining area also has wooden beams on the ceiling and a wooden island.

The bedrooms follow the home's minimalistic aesthetic and feature enough space for a queen-sized bed while boasting small windows.

"The residence blends historic authenticity with modern luxury, featuring wide-plank antique floors, exposed beams, preserved fireplaces, and original architectural details," the listing added.

The bathrooms feature double vanities, a large glass-enclosed shower, a marble soaking tub, and sliding barn doors.

Elsewhere, there is a gym, spa center with a massage chair, and an outdoor entertaining area with a foosball table.

Throughout the home, modern aesthetics have been meticulously merged with historic charm.

"A thoughtful renovation delivers elevated comfort throughout, including a newly created primary suite with cathedral ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows, a bespoke dressing room, and a private staircase to a serene, light-filled office and library retreat for everyday living," the listing stated.

Simms and his wife lived in Greenwich for many years, having previously sold another dwelling in the area for $2.7 million before relocating to their farmhouse.

They chose the farmhouse for its impressive parcel, noting to the outlet that they wanted more space for their horses.

However, they are now choosing to call to New York home.

Before settling down in Connecticut, Simms enjoyed a lengthy career in the NFL, a career that began at the University of Texas at Austin, after which he was drafted by the Buccaneers as the last pick of the final round in the 2003 NFL draft.

Simms remained with Tampa Bay until 2008, when he was released by the team. He was later picked up by the Tennessee Titans, with whom he played for a year before moving on to the Denver Broncos.

After a brief return to the Titans, the quarterback's career came to an end, with many pointing to a 2006 spleen injury as the reason for his retirement from the NFL.

He briefly tried his hand at coaching, signing with the New England Patriots in 2012 as an offensive coach, as well as a scouting expert, but he made a move into broadcasting after just a few months.

Simms and his wife, who met in high school, tied the knot in 2004 and now share two children.

Although Hilton insisted he has "nothing but wonderful memories" while calling Nevada home, he claimed that his decision to relocate to the Sunshine State came from a higher power.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.
  • Sources indicate that smith Point Capital led the Series A round.
  • Recent findings suggest that many industrial machinery malfunctions affect internal components that aren’t visible to an outside observer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:37 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.

Sources indicate that smith Point Capital led the Series A round. BrightAI said in its Wednesday announcement of the deal that a number of other venture capital firms contributed as well. They were joined by GE Vernova Inc., an energy equipment company that emerged from the 2024 split-up of General Electric Co.

Recent findings suggest that many industrial machinery malfunctions affect internal components that aren’t visible to an outside observer. As a result, problems often go unnoticed until they cause a major disruption. Palo Alto, California-based BrightAI develops hardware and software tools that help customers spot issues earlier.

The first component of the company’s product portfolio is a collection of sensors called State Stickers. They’re small, rectangular devices with a ruggedized case and a long battery life. Technicians can attach them to industrial equipment to monitor for issues that can’t be detected visually.

According to recent reports, the motion of a machine’s internal components produces noise and  vibrations that tend to follow a specific pattern. If an industrial fan’s blades rotate 30 times per minute, it might give off a whooshing sound every two seconds. BrightAI’s State Stickers can detect when a machine diverges from its usual operating pattern.

Sources indicate that the sensors wirelessly transmit their measurements to a device called the Stateful AI Hub. It runs artificial intelligence models that analyze the data for signs of hardware failures. According to the company, its models become more accurate as the number of sensors deployed at a site grows.

In a recent development, brightAI offers software that enables companies to augment the data from its sensors with drone footage. A utility, for  example, could use a BrightAI-powered drone to detect erosion at the top of an electric pole. The firm’s AI models automatically draw a square around damaged components to spare technicians the hassle of manually analyzing footage.

Sources indicate that the company claims that its software can also collect maintenance data in other ways. A BrightAI-powered drone can read the meters that are attached to assets such as data center coolant tanks to check their internal pressure. Furthermore, built-in support for infrared cameras enables the software to spot overheating equipment.

The third core component of BrightAI’s product portfolio is an AI wearable. The Stateful Wearable, as it’s called, provides technicians with troubleshooting advice in the field. It also checks whether they follow safety guidelines during inspections and automatically turns maintenance data into reports.

“Our infrastructure is under more strain than it has ever been, and Physical AI has finally become reliable enough to work in the field,” said founder and Chief Executive Alex Hawkinson. “Bringing those two facts together is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.”.

It has been revealed that brightAI says that its products monitor hundreds of thousands of industrial assets across 50,000 sites. Investor GE Vernova, which is also a customer, plans to expand its use of the manufacturer’s technology in connection with this week’s funding round. BrightAI, for its part, will use the capital to grow its international presence.

#30390. The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realtor ↗ Open Full Page

The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.
  • Many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home.
  • Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.

Many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home. But that's not necessarily true.

Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.

These programs can help buyers snag a home by providing cash that can go toward a down payment. There are even loan programs for certain qualified buyers that don't require any down payments. The array of offerings from federal, local, and private sources can take the form of looser loan requirements, outright grants of money, or tax credits, all of which make homeownership more affordable.

Industry observers note that first-time homebuyers, often with certain qualifications, are often beneficiaries of the assistance. Lower-income buyers, those who serve in the military or are veterans, and those who purchase fixer-uppers or homes in rural areas might also be eligible for the help.

The assistance ranges greatly, from a grant of several thousand dollars to, at the high end, a savings of five figures over the life of the loan.

Down payment assistance can take several forms and can even help buyers circumvent the PMI payment.

While 20% down has been something of a gold standard for homebuyers, it's also the minimum that generally lets them avoid private mortgage insurance, or PMI, which is assessed because lenders believe the loan carries risk. This in turn raises the homebuyer’s monthly expenses.

Here's an example: PMI is typically 0.5% to 1% of the loan amount per year. So if buyers put down less than 20% and their mortgage is $300,000, their PMI would be between $1,500 and $3,000 per year. That would add about $125 to $250 per month on top of their mortgage payment, a significant charge. (Homeowners can have PMI canceled when the equity in their home surpasses 20%.).

It has been revealed that so, while a buyer can also choose loans that require a down payment of just a single digit, that PMI can stretch a budget paper-thin. That's where down payment assistance can help.

It has been revealed that at least 2,000 such programs exist across the country. Some are federal, but most tend to be at state and local levels, which is crucial to know when searching for help. Private organizations, from lenders to nonprofits, also work with borrowers who need help.

Industry observers note that these programs might offer grants, loans, tax credits, or a combination of a couple of these benefits. Funding can come from our government, nonprofits, and private enterprises. Let’s take a closer look:.

Grants might be the most desirable form of down payment assistance. Typically, a grant is fully forgiven at closing and never has to be paid back. Yes, we’re talking about free money!

In a recent development, about 7% of down payment help comes in the form of grants, notes Veronica Khandelwal, vice president of HFA Relations at Down Payment Resource, which provides consumers with guidance on this kind of assistance. But there is a catch.

Sources indicate that “Grants require owner occupancy," she claims of the requirement for buyers to live in these properties. That's to make sure these loans don't go to investors or vacation-home buyers. "Some programs allow grants to be applied to multifamily purchases of one to four units so long as one of the units is occupied by the borrower.".

It has been revealed that forgivable loans are another option. These loans need to be repaid only if a repayment trigger event occurs, such as the home being sold before the end of the term, the home being no longer owner-occupied, the title being transferred, or the loan being defaulted on.

Deferred-payment loans are also available. These are paid back either at the end of the loan term or if a repayment trigger occurs. So, while it’s not a gift, it will help homebuyers get over that down payment hurdle and buy a house they might otherwise not have been able to afford.

Repayable loans are another leg up on homeownership. They require borrowers to make monthly payments, like a typical loan. But here's the good part: They do so at interest rates starting as low as 0%. That helps spread the down payment and closing costs over a number of years, making it much easier to enter the housing market.

Industry observers note that some agencies also offer a combination of these forms of assistance. That could mean that a portion of the help will be forgiven (or “written off” with no repayment needed), while some will need to be repaid. Tax credits are sometimes offered as well, further sweetening the deal.

Each down payment assistance program will have its own rules and guidelines, but the vast majority are offered only for a home that buyers will live in as a primary residence.

Here are some of the more popular national options folks might access to help them to pivot from home shopper to homebuyer.

FHA (Federal Housing Authority) loans were created by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for first-time homeowners (HUD). These mortgages allow as little as 3.5% for the down payment, provided buyers have a credit score of 580 or higher, along with other qualifying factors. The federal government insures these loans, and for that reason, banks are more willing to loan money to homebuyers who have neither top-tier credit nor loads of cash to put down on the purchase.

Industry observers note that FHA Section 203(k) loans require only 3% down, provided qualifying buyers will live in the property, typically one that needs work, while they fix it up. For buyers hoping for a DIY route into a dream home, this could be a win-win. The cost of improvements is included in the loan so buyers can finance both the home and up to $35,000 in repairs.

But buyers beware: The cost of materials and construction labor has spiked since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and work is taking much longer to be completed than ever before.

Sources indicate that VA (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) loans might be offered directly by the VA or backed by the department. Several factors are considered, such as service history, duty status, income, and credit rating. But those who qualify can purchase a home with zero down as long as the sales price isn’t higher than the home’s appraised value.

In a recent development, fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are federally funded loans that can help buyers skirt steep down payments. The Home Possible, HomeReady, and HomeOne loans typically offer a 3% down payment mortgage to qualifying, lower-income homebuyers.

According to recent reports, good Neighbor Next Door is another HUD-sponsored program. In this case, law enforcement officers, teachers, firefighters, and emergency medical technicians can enjoy a substantial incentive in the form of a discount of 50% from the list price of the home in a community that is being revitalized. The buyer must live in the house for three years as a primary residence.

Industry observers note that teacher Next Door Grant is a program similar to the one above but is designed to help educators own their own homes. Grants to the tune of up to $8,000 in certain areas are possible with additional down payment assistance available in some circumstances.

Sources indicate that the USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) Rural Home Loan Program was created to assist people buying homes in rural locations. For qualifying, single-family properties, loans might be available with no money down. There are maximum income limits and other qualifications to be eligible for one of these mortgages.

Industry observers note that there are plenty of other programs available as well. Different states and cities, as well as individual lenders and nonprofits, can help prospective homebuyers get the financing they need. Folks should put their location and "down payment assistance" into a search engine, and take a look at what's available. They might see everything from Habitat for Humanity to local religious organizations pop up. Also,visit Down Payment Resource.

Sources indicate that one other path to explore is whether a buyer's job provides down payment assistance. A lot of employers may offer assistance in  the form of a $10,000 loan that is forgivable after five years.

Recent findings suggest that down payments hit a four-year low at the start of 2026. The median payment fell to $23,400 and 12.8% in Q1 2026, down 19% and 1.2 ppts year over year.

However, down payments remain well above pre-pandemic levels, as more buying is happening in the lower-down-payment South and Midwest, even as the Northeast stays deeply competitive.

In a recent development, the Northeast posted the highest median down payment at $57,600, reflecting higher home prices and more competition. The Northeast also sees the largest gap between what buyers are paying as a down payment today compared to pre-pandemic.

Sources indicate that compared to 2019, the Northeast has seen down payments climb 236.8%, significantly more than the next closest gap of 134.0% in the Midwest. These trends are consistent with the persistent upward pressure on home prices in these regions as scarce inventory is met with sustained buyer demand.

Get ready for some good news. There are a lot of misconceptions about who qualifies for down payment assistance.

In a recent development, “Many people think these programs are only available to low-income borrowers, first-time homebuyers, or for properties that have sales price limits,” states Down Payment Resource's Khandelwal. “But if you look, you’ll find specialized programs designed to assist specific groups, including first-generation homebuyers, minorities, Indigenous people, people of color, veterans, those with government jobs, disabilities, and more.”.

Here’s something else to smile about: A first-time homebuyer doesn't just mean someone who's never bought a home before.

The federal government generally holds a broader definition of a first-time homebuyer. It’s someone who has not been a homeowner in the past three years. If you sold a house three-and-a-half years ago, you qualify as first-time buyer.

Buyers can take several different steps to find a down payment assistance program that’s right for them.

Check the federal programs mentioned above (like HUD, VA, USDA, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac), and see if there’s anything suitable.

In a recent development, buyers should also visit their state’s Department of Housing website and see what might be listed, or call their number and inquire what down payment assistance programs might be available. Cities, towns, private lenders, and nonprofits may also have help.

“Homebuyers should seek the assistance of a mortgage lender who specializes in affordable lending to identify their best options,” advises Khandelwal.

In a recent development, in terms of what is typically needed to access aid, the documentation is very much in line with what’s needed to apply for any mortgage. Buyers will likely need the following:.

Pay stubs plus W-2s from the past few years to verify employment and income history.

Any 1099 forms showing other income.

Details on the property they intend to buy (The real estate agent can share this information.).

The paperwork is processed in much the same way as a home loan, and there may be requests for more documents.

Then, if buyers are approved, they will be ready to move ahead with a lower—or no—down payment as their homeownership journey unfolds.

Recent findings suggest that janet Siroto is a journalist, editor, and trend tracker. Her work has appeared in Cosmopolitan, Good Housekeeping, and other publications.

Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

📅 07 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtybiznews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients.
  • The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience.
  • Sources indicate that the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that owners will see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

Sources indicate that the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that owners will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

It has been revealed that when writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

In a recent development, storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

Sources indicate that in the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Industry observers note that social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

To encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

An effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt people to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Sources indicate that continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

It has been revealed that writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elle and Dakota Fanning have been in the spotlight for decades, but their upcoming project, “The Nightingale,” marks the first time they’ve played sisters onscreen—an experience that brought them “closer” together, both on set and at home.

While they’ve visited each other on set in the past and even separately played different versions of the same character in the 2001 film “I Am Sam,” Elle, 28, told Vanity Fair that actually working with each other is a totally different ball game.

It has been revealed that “It certainly brought us closer, which was hard to imagine—to be closer,” she said. “Our mom always left us little notes in suitcases, like, ‘Just savor this time together. This is precious.’”.

Dakota, 32, confirmed that they took their mother’s advice.

Recent findings suggest that “We did really savor it,” she stated. “And the biggest takeaway for me is when we have each other and when we’re together, we can do anything. That’s really how I feel. There’s nothing that I couldn’t do with Elle there with me.”.

That said, the job wasn’t easy. The Fannings traveled to Budapest to shoot on location, where they lived together.

“It was a challenging shoot, not going to lie. It was physically tiring, certainly emotionally taxing,” said Elle.

After a long day of using lots of “brain power” on set, the sisters had to find a way to “recharge” each evening.

For Dakota and Elle, that meant eating lots of Thai food and streaming “The Real Housewives,” true crime, and “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”—the TV series the younger sister stars in, which was released while they filmed “The Nightingale.”.

Dakota revealed that on a day off, she’d often find herself cleaning up after Elle, which was poetic as her character, Vianne, also tidies her sister Isabelle’s mess.

In a recent development, “Her bed in the mornings is like a tornado has run through it,” she mentioned. “She’s just one of those sleepers. It’s all twisted into a crazy thing. I was like, ‘That’s no fun to get into a bed that’s all crumpled and rumpled. Let me make it nice.’”.

The older sister said that “it became a routine,” and she “always made her bed like that” when possible.

Elle mentioned, “It’s art imitating life, because there’s even a scene where Vianne is making Isabelle’s bed, too.”.

According to recent reports, dakota and Elle were born in Conyers, GA. As young girls, they traveled between the Atlanta suburb and Los Angeles to work before relocating to the West Coast full time.

“When we were younger, we wanted to make sure that people saw us differently, and we wanted to give each other space to carve our own path,” Elle told Vanity Fair in 2025. “But as adults, it’s been very fulfilling to merge.”.

One of the most major ways the sisters have merged their lives in adulthood was in 2017, when they purchased a gorgeous $2.3 million property together.

According to Architectural Digest, they lived in a Cape Cod-style home in the Valley Village area of San Fernando Valley.

The 4,550-square-foot residence was perched at the end of a private, gated driveway and had a very classic aesthetic with white rose bushes planted along the front walkway.

The interiors were defined by delicate details, such as baby blue brocade-patterned walls, intricate chandeliers, and coffered ceilings.

The sisters sold the six-bedroom, six-bathroom estate for just under $2.7 million in May 2020.

It’s clear that Dakota was a fan of the dwelling’s traditional style, as she bought a very similar-looking home in Toluca Lake for $2.95 million in 2019, just before offloading the property she shared with Elle.

According to recent reports, according to Architectural Digest, Dakota’s newer home spans 4,428 square feet and boasts five bedrooms and six bathrooms. It’s flooded with natural light and, like the first home, has crystal chandeliers, a pool in the backyard, and a double-height entry hall.

  • According to a Page Six report, Trujillo's new pad is a $1.1 million condo he purchased in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four months after announcing their split, “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City” cast member Angie Katsanevas and her estranged husband, Shawn Trujillo, are now living in separate homes.

“Recently, Shawn has bought a place that’s two minutes down the street. And I’m at home with Elektra,” Katsanevas revealed in a fresh People magazine interview.

According to a Page Six report, Trujillo's new pad is a $1.1 million condo he purchased in September. The two-story dwelling spans 2,568 square feet and includes three bedrooms and 4.5 bathrooms.

The couple, who married in June 1999, have yet to legally divorce, but are "moving toward" that status.

“We are separated. We haven’t put it on paper, but we are not reconciling as far as staying married,” the reality TV star, 53, explained. “I hate the big D-word, but I’ll just have to say that, yeah, we are moving toward the big D.”.

The salon owner’s home—which viewers will recognize from the reality series—is a sprawling hillside estate that has been on and off the market for the past two years.

Recent findings suggest that the four-bedroom, three-bathroom modern abode was first listed for $4.5 million in September 2024. The price was decreased to $4.38 million in March 2025, then to $3.85 million just two months later.

By December of last year, the listing was removed. It hit the market again in January 2026 for $3.85 million, where it sat for most of the year before being removed on Oct. 14.

The couple purchased the 6,369-square-foot residence for an undisclosed sum in 2020. With soaring ceilings, white ash floors, and lots of sleek, marble surfaces, the modern abode has a distinct luxurious aesthetic.

The home has two primary suites, with one that includes a fireplace, sitting area, and double-vanity bathroom with a striking view of the surrounding Utah landscape. There are also dual walk-in closets.

The second is located on the main floor and also has two-walk in closets and a gorgeous bathroom.

In a recent development, features in pairs seem to be a feature of the home in general, as there are also two kitchens. In addition to the chic white minimalist space at the center of the home, a concealed catering kitchen is equipped with Miele appliances, a separate refrigerator and freezer, and a space for staff to prepare food.

It seems as if, despite the separation, daily life hasn’t changed too much in the home. Katsanevas noted that Trujillo stops by most days to pick up their 15-year-old daughter, Elektra, and take her to school.

“He’ll come in and have coffee,” she explained. “He’ll bring her home from lessons, and we’ll have dinner together. We are still just spending time together. We’re best friends. We are peaceful, it’s positive. We have a lot to do together.”.

She noted that Trujillo remains close with her father and will celebrate the holidays with the family.

“My dad sends him all of his favorite dishes and continues to cook for him,” said Katsanevas. “Shawn will spend Thanksgiving and Christmas with my family.”.

Although they are still connected in many ways, Katsanevas noted that after nearly three decades together, “space and doing things independently” have brought clarity.

“We are even going to different churches now,” she shared. “And that’s huge for me. We started out going to the same church.”.

Katsanevas also shut down rumors that she had initiated the split over their opposing political stances, a rumor that started after she cited their “different views” in a confessional interview during a recent episode of “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City.”.

In a recent development, “I’m not throwing a 30-year marriage away because of rumors or political views,” she mentioned. “There are so many things that Shawn and I have grown apart and have different views on, a lot of things at this stage of life. And it’s not one thing. It’s just, we’re very different people.”.

They’re still business partners, however, and are set to open a latest hair salon together in Miami.

“We are continuing to grow our brand together, even though we are separated,” she noted.

Katsanevas and Trujillo at the moment operate nine locations of their business, Lunatic Fringe Salon, across Utah, Ohio, and Idaho.

While she’s focused on remaining positive, Katsanevas mentioned it took some time to work through the complicated feelings that accompanied the change.

According to recent reports, “It does take a minute to mourn the loss of the way your life once was and what it looked like,” she said. “I’ve processed, I’ve cried, I’ve accepted. I’ve had to swim away from the muddy waters to get to the clear water and say, ‘OK, I’m coming out of this and I’m going to be OK.’”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic’s initial public offering priced above expectations for its IPO on Thursday, with the organization’s fully diluted valuation coming to roughly $1.494 trillion—more than the total residential real estate values in many entire states.
  • It has been revealed that the Claude developer, which will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, priced at $83 a share, above the predicted $70 to $78 range.
  • To help better understand the massive $1.494 trillion price tag, Realtor.com® put the number in terms of real estate—and the statistics are shocking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic’s initial public offering priced above expectations for its IPO on Thursday, with the organization’s fully diluted valuation coming to roughly $1.494 trillion—more than the total residential real estate values in many entire states.

It has been revealed that the Claude developer, which will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, priced at $83 a share, above the predicted $70 to $78 range. The firm sold 980 million Class A shares, raising an initial $81 billion and shattering SpaceX’s $72 billion record.

To help better understand the massive $1.494 trillion price tag, Realtor.com® put the number in terms of real estate—and the statistics are shocking.

San Francisco is a longtime hot spot for tech giants. It saw the growth of Google and Facebook, and has now become the landing spot for Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI startups. The constant stream of tech wealth, combined with a limited number of desirable homes, has created a competitive market. San Francisco County has a median sales price of $1.6 million, and yet, Anthropic blows the entire market out of the water.

Recent findings suggest that the aggregate value of every home for sale in San Francisco is a mere $8.6 billion, a small fraction of Anthropic's new valuation. Indeed, the total value of every owner-occupied home in the San Francisco metro is $1.37 trillion, according to the 2-25 American Community Survey. Anthropic’s valuation exceeds that by about $123 billion.

This trend is consistent in 391 metros out of 393.

The only two metros with more owner-occupied home value than Anthropic is worth are Latest York City, at $3.26 trillion, and Los Angeles, at $2.64 trillion.

Furthermore, the AI giant’s valuation tops the owner-occupied home value in 46 out of the 50 states, as well as Washington, DC.

The value of all owner-occupied homes in the state of New Jersey comes in at $1.44 trillion, just shy of Anthropic’s valuation.

Recent findings suggest that throughout the country, all owner-occupied homes are worth $43.6 trillion. Anthropic’s valuation equals about 3.4% of all owner-occupied housing wealth in the United States.

When it comes to homes on the market, Anthropic’s valuation stacks up high.

In a recent development, across the U.S., about 1.18 million homes are for sale, listed for a combined $816 billion. Anthropic’s valuation could snap up every single one and still have $678 billion left.

Even without the first $1 trillion of the valuation, the remaining $494 billion could buy every home for sale in the 20 metros with the highest total listing value with billions to spare: about 372,000 homes listed at a combined $356 billion.

According to recent reports, as Anthropic’s debut is discussed, the valuation may be rounded to $1.49 trillion, as it’s common for financial figures to be kept to one or two digits. However, that dropped digit in the $1.494 trillion figure is $4 billion. That rounding error alone is greater than the combined value of every owner-occupied home in Racine, WI, which total $3.97 billion.

That same $4 billion could buy every home for sale in Alaska: 2,196 listings worth $1.16 billion. For a change in scenery, it could then cover every home for sale on Kauai, the Kapa’a, Hawaii, market, which has 356 listings worth $925 million, and still have about $1.9 billion left to purchase all the homes for sale in the Boulder, CO, metro area.

It’s no wonder the AI boom is reshaping markets in tech hubs like Upcoming York City and San Francisco, when the valuation of just one firm looms so high.

UPDATED 20:48 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

A bipartisan group of more than two dozen congressional lawmakers mentioned today they’re forming a new AI Safety and Innovation Caucus to tackle the growing security risks posed by the advances in sophisticated artificial intelligence models.

The lawmakers cited the July hack of Hugging Face Inc.’s servers by a team of autonomous AI agents developed by OpenAI Group PBC, which broke out of an isolated sandbox environment, as an example of these risks. They also pointed to another incident involving the now-public Anthropic PBC, which also reported that its agents escaped their testing environments to access third-party systems.

Recent findings suggest that these incidents have “underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions,” remarked Representative George Whitesides (D-California), a co-chair of the caucus. “As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems and threats to national security.”.

In a recent development, whitesides (pictured) is co-chairing the caucus alongside Representatives Nathanial Moran (R-TX) and Don Beyer (D-Virginia). In a post on X, they stressed the need for bipartisan collaboration to create the basic policy guardrails for AI safety, citing the growing concerns of the American public.

According to recent reports, does it feel like there's a new tech or AI crisis every day? Recent headlines are raising serious concerns about our digital safety and security.

Today, I'm joining @RepDonBeyer, @RepNateMoran, and over 20 of our colleagues to launch the bipartisan AI Safety and Innovation… pic.twitter.com/bhMyygy1J6.

Recent findings suggest that — Rep. George Whitesides (@Rep_Whitesides) November 19, 2026.

The 26-member caucus includes seven Republicans, which is a surprising number given that the White House administration under President Donald Trump has strongly opposed any heavy-handed regulation of the AI industry. The goal of the caucus is to identify “targeted solutions” that ensure AI remains under control without derailing innovation and threatening America’s lead in the industry.

Whitesides mentioned the lawmakers will focus on two things: proposing legislation to augment AI safety, and responding rapidly to high-profile security incidents by gathering developers, independent experts and government officials to brief lawmakers and come up with solutions.

“We want to be a conduit through which effective, responsible legislation can be refined and brought to the floor of the House,” Whitesides told Politico in an interview. He noted the group will work together to propose, provide feedback and endorse latest AI legislation. He believes there’s an urgent need for this, because most other groups within the House are more focused on educating members or creating legislation within their own parties, he said.

According to recent reports, another thing the caucus intends to do is to pursue relationships with outside AI experts who can help lawmakers to navigate complex policy decisions. It also wants to help raise public awareness around AI and its safety complications, and ensure members outside of relevant committees have the tools they need to contribute to latest legislation and debate.

In the recent midterm elections, Americans made it clear that AI is becoming a major concern for governance. Moreover, a recent survey revealed that 43% of Americans don’t trust either of the two major political parties to properly get a grip on AI safety, according to a one-pager that accompanied the press release.

Sources indicate that “Artificial intelligence affects every American, and it should not be a partisan issue,” Moran mentioned. “This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe. Congress needs to be prepared.”.

Netflix dropped the Season 10 trailer on Nov. 18, and in one heated exchange, Christine and Heather’s conflict comes to a head.

In a recent development, the pair have been at odds for quite some time, facing multiple tense on-screen moments. In a 2023 E! News interview, Christine branded Heather “a snooze fest,” claiming she’s not interesting enough for TV.

Then, in a July 2026 clip from E!, Heather revealed that prior to filming Season 10, she had not seen or spoken to Christine in four years.

“You literally said you hated me,” Christine pressed in the trailer.

Instead of shying away from the confrontation, Heather fessed up.

“At that point, Christine, I did,” she admitted.

In another scene, Heather opens up to her husband, Tarek El Moussa, sharing insight on the challenging dynamic between the women.

“It was a big decision for me to even start working in the office again,” noted Heather, noting that “obviously,” she has her “guard up” with Christine and still feels she can’t “trust her.”.

“She’s gone through some sh-t,” Tarek responded. “That previous Christine is still this newly introduced Christine.”.

Sources indicate that despite the tension, both women seem to be excited for the upcoming season, which premieres on Dec. 4.

Sources indicate that in a since-expired Instagram Story, Heather said, “The trailer is so good. I watched it like 10 times.”.

Christine meanwhile wrote “We’re SOOO back!” in a comment on a Netflix post sharing a condensed-version of the trailer.

Both women opened up to Netflix’s publication, Tudum, ahead of the fresh season.

“I finally feel secure enough in who I am to walk back into that world and not lose myself in it,” Heather remarked.

Sources indicate that the proud mom left The Oppenheim Group after Season 7 to focus on family after welcoming her first child with Tarek—a son named Tristan Jay, now 3. Heather is also a co-parent to her husband’s two older children, Taylor Reese, 16, and Brayden James, 11, whom he shares with his ex-wife, Christina Haack.

In a recent development, “I want people to see the full picture of who I am now,” she continued. “Not just the dramatic moments. The version of me returning is very different from the one who left.”.

In the interview, Heather teased, “there are conversations that got cut short,” that there are some things she’s “not going to pretend” haven’t happened.

Meanwhile, Christine parted ways with the brokerage at the end of Season 5, after welcoming her son, Christian Georges Dumontet, whom she shares with her estranged husband, Christian Dumontet.

“Motherhood has a way of sharpening your priorities and changing how you move through the world,” she told Tudum. “I’ve become more intentional and much more protective of my peace.”.

With that mentioned, Christine doesn’t initiative to steer clear of all conflict.

“I’m still ambitious and direct, but I think people will see a version of me that’s more centered and even more sure of herself,” she explained. “I’m hoping this chapter feels fresh and honest.”.

It has been revealed that season 10 will also see the return of agents Bre Tiesi and Amanza Smith. Four latest professionals will join the group, too: Jordyn Taylor, Sasha Lance, Sonni Pacheco, and Tara Burns.

Sources indicate that jason Oppenheim, head of the brokerage, said, “The newly introduced agents have already shaken up the office, but in a good way. I absolutely love the new ladies, and they make me excited about the future here at the brokerage and on the show.”.

#30379. Why Do Empty-Nest Boomers Own So Many Homes in Top School Districts?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (956 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realtor ↗ Open Full Page

Why Do Empty-Nest Boomers Own So Many Homes in Top School Districts?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the best-performing school districts often bring stiff competition from families looking to break in, while older neighbors stay put.
  • The paper from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland studied the household characteristics of the best-performing school districts in the country, which command higher real estate prices but also a higher barrier to entry.
  • The Cleveland Fed's findings show that seniors occupy a larger share of households in good school districts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the best-performing school districts often bring stiff competition from families looking to break in, while older neighbors stay put. But helping free up housing in these districts isn't as simple as getting older people to move, a new study argues.

The paper from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland studied the household characteristics of the best-performing school districts in the country, which command higher real estate prices but also a higher barrier to entry.

The Cleveland Fed's findings show that seniors occupy a larger share of households in good school districts. But it pinned that on affordability challenges. Higher-income households of all types compete for housing in the best-performing school districts.

This is a conundrum for neighborhoods. Seniors are thus left in neighborhoods paying premiums for school districts they don't use. Meanwhile young families who'd like move into the district face limited options for homes there.

Of course, many seniors want to age in place in homes that they've lived in for decades. But others looking to downsize are "locked in" due to high mortgage rates. That can leave them in homes that they can't afford or, worse, in homes that pose safety risks for aging people.

"These findings suggest that policies aimed solely at encouraging older households to downsize are unlikely to substantially improve access to quality school districts," the paper claims.

Sources indicate that low housing turnover in these districts drives up prices. The higher-rated public school districts are, on average, 49% more expensive, and homes there move faster, Realtor.com® data indicates. But in some of the nation's top school districts—including in Dallas, Los Angeles, and San Fransisco—homes can sell for three times the price of surrounding metros.

Using data from the American Community Survey, the Cleveland Fed found that households over 65 occupy a disproportionate share of the housing stock in the best-performing school districts. While these account for 26.2% of all households nationally, they make up as much as 28.7% of households in the least affordable areas.

Meanwhile households with children, which make up about 31.2% of U.S. households, occupy 30.1% of housing in the best school districts and 40% of the housing stock in the lowest-quality districts. The same doesn't ring true for one-person households, which tend to be more evenly distributed.

Older homeowners move at about the same rate across all school districts—about 6.9% a year. About 81% of older adults in the best school districts own their homes. To the Cleveland Fed, that shows older households aren't limiting turnover of housing stock in high-quality and high-cost districts.

Sources indicate that "While older households occupy a modestly larger share of housing in these expensive, high-quality areas, they do not appear to limit turnover," the paper states. "These patterns suggest that the challenge of accessing high-quality school districts is driven by a combination of income sorting and competition from multiple household types rather than solely by empty-nesters’ aging in place.".

Realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu indicates a few concerns are affecting seniors as they consider their futures. They include capital gains taxes they'd incur on homes that have appreciated in value. They also include the kinds of taxes they'd incur when they move to a upcoming place. Then there are the social considerations.

It has been revealed that "Right-sized, single-level, accessible homes near family and doctors are scarce," Xu claims. "Moving also means leaving behind the neighbors and community that owners have built over decades. For many longtime owners, there are few good places to go.".

Industry observers note that buyers can still find deals in some of these good markets, Realtor.com found, if they look carefully. But in some good districts, there simply aren't a lot of homes changing hands.

Xu adds that she's surprised that young professionals without children can also compete for housing in these expensive districts. Jobs, urban amenities, and investment opportunity for the real estate tend to make these areas attractive.

"Even if more seniors moved, the homes they left would likely go to higher-income buyers, because this is a sorting story. The districts wouldn’t become much more affordable," Xu claims. "The more direct solution is building more homes in and near high-demand districts. Adding right-sized options could also give older owners who want to move somewhere to go, but supply is what would ease pressure on prices.".

To Arick Morton, CEO of NIC MAP, the frozen market points to a need for more housing oriented toward seniors. Earlier this year, his group said the nation needs to add 1 million new senior housing units by 2040. That $1 trillion homebuilding frenzy would meet the moment 10 million baby boomers pass age 80.

Sources indicate that "People stay at home much longer than they did previously," Morton said. "Of course folks stay at home as long as they can and then movie into senior housing when the need is there.".

But when there isn't enough senior housing or they don't have good alternatives to downsize, those seniors end up displaced when age or an accident means they require more intensive care needs.

"The best policy options are those that help expedite the construction of senior housing," Morton remarked. "We don't have enough capacity to create a dent in that logjam.".

Recent findings suggest that data center backlash is pushing builders to show communities what they get in return, and public-private partnerships are becoming one answer. As the race for sovereign AI heats up, the question is shifting from where intellectual property lives to where compute runs and who profits from it.

According to recent reports, canada offers a sharp test case. A modern data hall employs few people, but its profits can fund the startups and jobs a region needs, according to Sharif Virani (pictured), chief executive officer of SPUR Innovation Center.

It has been revealed that “There’s a massive misnomer right now in the world that’s kind of landing from previous tech, where people think where your IP is where the wealth creation is going to be,” he said. “It’s not the case anymore. You have to make sure your inference happens in your country or in your region.”.

Sources indicate that virani spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and host Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed sovereign AI, reinvesting data center profits in local entrepreneurs and winning over residents through public-private partnerships. (* Disclosure below.).

Recent findings suggest that SPUR treats its Waterloo, Ontario, site as an innovation campus with an attached data hall rather than a pure data center. The manufacturer reinvests about 10 percent of the campus’s data center profits in local entrepreneurs through a venture studio and takes first right of refusal on their office space and compute, Virani explained. Canada’s Dominion List counts more than 500 founders who have left for San Francisco, he noted.

Recent findings suggest that “We have entrepreneurship at an all-time low, productivity at an all-time low [and] GDP in freefall,” he mentioned. “That’s really the result. We’ve got to reverse that.”.

According to recent reports, one of SPUR’s early investments went to two international students who had full scholarships to the University of Toronto and internships lined up in San Francisco. Instead, they launched a startup called Auditorium AI and hired staff, according to Virani. The model also reaches Main Street, where on-campus hackathons helped a former long-haul trucker build AI software for logistics.

“AI allows these people who know the problem, who have earned the right to solve the problem, to mobilize technology to do it and make the lives of their friends, families and neighbors better,” Virani noted.

A real-life Barbie dream house is turning heads in Hudson, WI, where an eye-catching pink Victorian has gone under contract after hitting the market for $1.1 million in June 2026.

With its pink walkway, bubble gum–colored staircase, and vibrant interior, this seven-bedroom, 5,189-square-foot home is anything but ordinary.

But behind its playful Barbie-inspired appearance is a spacious historical residence built in 1900 that is packed with character, original details, and incredible versatility.

“An everyday buyer interested in a classic Victorian home might think this is a bit much,” says listing agent Jennifer R. Martin of Edina Realty Inc. “It has a lot of great qualities. I would say to anyone not to let the color deter you. Painting is easy, and it’s not that expensive to make changes.”.

It has been revealed that at the moment a successful short-term rental, the home is near the St. Croix River and could be used for multigenerational living or converted into a single-family home.

Sources indicate that “The sizing alone of the house is incredible,” Martin states. “It’s enormous and goes on forever. It has two separate kitchens, so it could also be turned into a duplex.”.

It is part of a collection of rose-hued homes operated by Fleetwood Rentals, which hosts everything from birthday parties to bachelorette weekends.

Industry observers note that “The seller’s clientele is looking for a party weekend destination,” she notes. “It’s one block from the riverfront and two blocks away from downtown.”.

Located 30 minutes from the Minneapolis/St. Paul airport, the property last changed hands for $614,000 in 2020. It offers “outstanding income potential,” the listing states.

“When the seller bought it, right away she had it painted in dark charcoal,” Martin says. “Her vision at that time was to have a Goth mansion that would be similar to Disney’s Haunted Mansion. It was right around the time the 'Barbie' movie was coming out, so she decided to take advantage of that.”.

The multilevel home also has formal and casual dining spaces and expansive gathering areas. Original details include woodwork, built-in cabinetry, vaulted ceilings, and dual staircases.

According to recent reports, "I envisioned the next buyer to be either another Airbnb owner or a large family who would un-pinkify it," Martin claims with a laugh. "It's a great house with a lot of great qualities. I told potential buyers not to let the color deter you.".

According to recent reports, the living room has pink walls, drapes, and couches. The formal dining room has built-in cabinetry and a fireplace. The light-filled kitchen, with an enormous breakfast bar, is a surprise with its white cabinetry and a copper farmhouse sink.

The bubble gum–painted grand staircase leads to the colorful sleeping quarters. Four bedrooms are on the second level and three more are on the third floor. The primary suite has a walk-in closet, a soaking tub, a separate glass shower, and a dual-sink vanity.

According to recent reports, other highlights include a home theater, a hot tub, a 14-foot swim spa, and a patio designed for entertaining. The fenced lot comes with a private patio, a two-car garage, and a driveway with parking for 12 vehicles.

The property is conveniently located near boutique shopping, riverfront parks, and the marina.

According to recent reports, "Hudson is a riverfront town with tons of history," Martin claims. "People love to come here for bachelorette parties and places to go out to dinner. It also has a lot of charming, fun shops.".

  • Bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes. Gold isn’t doing much better; oil and stocks have joined the sell-off. The markets are already nervous about the Federal Reserve’s next decision, and yesterday’s FOMC minutes gave us another reason to worry: policymakers are still talking about raising interest rates.

Industry observers note that almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate under their baseline outlook. Two even floated the possibility of a bigger increase if inflation refuses to cool.

This is a nasty combination for markets. Bitcoin fell around 3.2% over 24 hours, gold futures dropped more than 3%, and WTI crude lost around 3%. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Wall Street was mixed, though, with the Nasdaq finishing higher while the Dow and S&P 500 slipped.

Here’s the comparison. In March 2020, the Fed was slashing rates, buying bonds and throwing emergency liquidity at a financial system under immense pressure. Congress approved a $2.2 trillion rescue package to keep households and businesses afloat.

Today, we are watching markets fall while the Fed is possibly making money more expensive.

October’s FOMC minutes weren’t exactly what markets wanted to hear. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% during its October meeting, but almost all participants believed further increases would likely be appropriate. Two officials also noted a hike larger than the usual 25 basis points could be considered if inflation data came in hotter than expected.

Recent findings suggest that and there was more in those minutes than just interest rates. Officials raised concerns about hedge fund leverage and the growing debt tied to artificial intelligence investments. Some financing arrangements could become a problem if investors start questioning enormous AI spending, and whether it will generate the returns companies expect.

In a recent development, the risk is forced selling. Leveraged funds facing losses or investor withdrawals may have to dump assets quickly, potentially pushing prices down further.

Sources indicate that gold has its own problem. A stronger dollar and higher interest rates make it less attractive to investors who can earn a return elsewhere. Bitcoin price, meanwhile, remains vulnerable when traders cut exposure to speculative assets.

According to recent reports, the Fed hasn’t declared a financial emergency. Its minutes actually describe the banking system as resilient. But officials are clearly paying attention to risks that could amplify a market shock.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

March 2020 was brutal. COVID-19 lockdowns brought businesses to a standstill. Investors rushed for cash, stocks collapsed, and Bitcoin briefly slipped below $4,000 after sitting near $10,000 just weeks earlier.

Sources indicate that the Federal Reserve didn’t wait around. It cut rates by 50 basis points on March 3, then delivered another 100-basis-point cut on March 15. The federal funds target range dropped to 0%–0.25%.

Industry observers note that on March 23, the Fed revealed unlimited purchases of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities, promising to buy whatever amounts were necessary to support market functioning. It also introduced emergency lending programmes to keep credit flowing.

According to recent reports, president Donald Trump signed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act on March 27. The package included direct payments to eligible Americans, expanded unemployment benefits, and assistance for businesses struggling to survive lockdowns. The Paycheck Protection Program gave small businesses access to loans designed to help them keep employees on payroll.

According to recent reports, the response was enormous, but the economy was facing an extraordinary shutdown. Millions of Americans had lost their jobs, businesses were closing, and normal economic activity had practically disappeared.

Industry observers note that markets eventually bounced back. The S&P 500 recovered its pre-pandemic record by August 2020. Bitcoin climbed above $12,000 during the same month.

The current US economy isn’t in the same position as it was during the pandemic. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, and policymakers are discussing rate increases rather than cuts.

Recent findings suggest that slashing rates to zero and flooding markets with liquidity might help asset prices. It could also make inflation worse. Another multitrillion-dollar spending package would face an entirely different argument in Congress, especially without a pandemic-style economic shutdown.

The Fed doesn’t have to choose between doing nothing and repeating the 2020 rescue. If banks struggle to fund themselves or credit markets start freezing, it can step in with emergency lending and liquidity operations. That’s a much narrower response than another round of unlimited bond purchases.

Recent findings suggest that the Fed’s concerns about leveraged hedge funds and AI financing could become more relevant if investors start selling indiscriminately. A market correction is one thing. Forced selling spreading through the financial system is another.

Sources indicate that at the moment, there’s no evidence that we’re facing another March 2020. The banking system remains resilient, and falling Bitcoin prices alone won’t trigger a government bailout.

But the Fed has a problem that didn’t exist in quite the same way during the pandemic. It may need to protect financial stability without giving up its fight against inflation. In 2020, Washington opened the taps. This time, we wait and see, and Bitcoin price will survive.
