Latest Update: Glenn Kelman’s next act: Former Redfin CEO takes on health care with stealthy startup Sojourn

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 8:34 amNovember 17, 2026 at 9:41 am.
  • Glenn Kelman famously told “60 Minutes” in 2007, “Real estate, by far, is the most screwed up industry in America.” It looks like health care is next on his list.
  • The former Redfin CEO has co-founded Sojourn, a Seattle startup that aims to give working people “better healthcare at a lower cost,” according to its website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 8:34 amNovember 17, 2026 at 9:41 am.

Glenn Kelman famously told “60 Minutes” in 2007, “Real estate, by far, is the most screwed up industry in America.” It looks like health care is next on his list.

The former Redfin CEO has co-founded Sojourn, a Seattle startup that aims to give working people “better healthcare at a lower cost,” according to its website.

“Since technology by itself can’t fix a broken system, we’re rebuilding the whole system to make it work for you — combining a software firm, a group of doctors and nurses, and an insurance company,” reads the introductory message on the site.

His co-founder is Dr. Connie Chen, an internist who co-founded digital health manufacturer Vida Health and spent more than seven years at mental health benefits company Lyra Health, first as chief medical officer and then as chief operating officer, as Lyra grew to a $5.6 billion valuation.

This is not a modest app for booking doctor’s appointments. Under the corporate name Silica Health Inc., the company filed a trademark application last month covering health maintenance organization services — HMOs are health aims that pair insurance coverage with their own networks of doctors — along with insurance administration, medical billing and claims management.

Kelman, who is rarely at a loss for words, confirmed in response to our inquiry that he wasn’t ready to talk yet. He wrote in a GeekWire guest column this month that he and his business partner would announce their plans “after we’ve built our product.”.

It has been revealed that but after he posted about his team on LinkedIn last week, we got curious and couldn’t help but look around. Their resumes were a tip-off: In addition to Chen, the team includes an engineer who spent nearly seven years at tech-driven health insurer Oscar Health.

Searching Kelman’s name in state business licenses turned up Silica Health, with Kelman and Chen listed as officers. Plugging that name into the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s database produced exactly one result: the application for “Sojourn Health.”.

From there, it was a short trip to sojournhealth.com, which sketches out the plan.

Why health care: Kelman spent 20 years running Redfin, which stood out in the real estate industry for employing its agents rather than treating them as independent contractors. That turns out to be part of the origin story.

According to recent reports, “Almost every year after its IPO, Redfin had to re-consider whether to keep employing its own agents, because of their rising healthcare costs,” Sojourn’s founders page explains. The options were to make agents contractors, ask employees to pay more, or cover less care.

“The choices were all terrible,” it says.

Chen’s bio on the site describes a career spent on one problem: how employers can give their employees better care at lower cost.

As a primary-care doctor, she saw her patients’ health and finances rise and fall together, the site indicates, and concluded that “a system taped together from broken parts couldn’t serve either.”.

It has been revealed that kelman, by his own account, is fresh to the field. In his guest column, he wrote that when he thought about the companies he would have been proud to start, they were all in one particular industry. He didn’t say which one, but it’s not hard to guess now.

“I had no experience in that industry, but a friend said I could offset that if I were willing to give it everything I have, which is what I’m now doing,” he wrote.

The team: In a LinkedIn post last week, Kelman remarked the founding team also includes Jennifer Chao and Ben Baker, with Sasha Aickin “adding some part-time magic.” He promised that “the mission is good and the ambition is vast.”.

The lineup draws on Kelman’s past and the health insurance world:.

Sources indicate that chao and Aickin both worked with Kelman at Plumtree Software, the enterprise software manufacturer he co-founded in 1996, before following him to Redfin. Sojourn’s recruiting page nods to the pattern: “We’re honored by the old friends who have worked with us from company to company, but we’re also eager to bring in new blood.”.

The Sojourn site says the company is likely to have engineering hubs in Seattle for the member experience, San Francisco for the clinical platform, and Austin for the claims system.

AI all the way down: Sojourn is hiring software engineers and product managers “at every level of the organization.” The first thing on its list of qualifications: experience using frontier AI tools “to generate reliable, high-scale production code.”.

According to recent reports, that fits with his guest column. A recruiter told him Seattle’s startup scene was “dead,” he wrote, and a friend described CTOs who were miserable trying to do “AI transformations” at companies with old code. Kelman wrote that “the logical response to all this has been to start an AI-native company in Seattle.”.

What we don’t know: The website doesn’t say when Sojourn plans to launch or where it will offer coverage first, although Chen’s bio suggests employers will be key customers, describing a care model “designed around the member and the employer who pays for it.”.

A fresh health plan typically requires state insurance licenses and significant capital reserves, and the tech giant hasn’t disclosed any funding. Kelman wrote in his column that he “met amazing, generous investors who gave me a good idea,” but he didn’t name them, and a search of SEC filings for Sojourn Health and Silica Health found no record of a fundraise.

In June, he joined venture firm Greylock as an executive in residence, saying at the time that he was still looking to start a new mission-driven enterprise, a process that involved “exploring ideas that are never going to work and howling at the moon.” It’s not clear whether Greylock is among his backers.

Sources indicate that kelman stepped down as Redfin CEO in January, six months after Rocket Companies completed its $1.75 billion acquisition of the Seattle brokerage. He remarked at the time that he wanted to find “another mission-driven enterprise outside of real estate.”.

He appears to have found one. Whether health care is more or less screwed up than real estate is a question that will have to wait until he’s ready to chat.

  • The latest on-chain data from Etherscan demonstrates that Shiba Inu has seen a rapid surge in adoption, with its number of on-chain holders surpassing 1.7 million for the first time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although Shiba Inu has continued to struggle amid the persisting market volatility, showing substantial daily losses, the leading meme token has just reached a major milestone in its holder count.

The latest on-chain data from Etherscan demonstrates that Shiba Inu has seen a rapid surge in adoption, with its number of on-chain holders surpassing 1.7 million for the first time.

While this has been a long-anticipated milestone in the SHIB community, the data has drawn attention across the market as it demonstrates that SHIB now has about 1,700,247 holders as of Tuesday, November 17.

Reaching a 1.7 million holder count at a time like this, when the market is facing extreme volatility, marks a major milestone for the SHIB ecosystem as it signals its growing appeal despite unfavorable market conditions.

Nonetheless, it is important to note that the number of holders alone does not necessarily indicate an increase in unique individual investors, as existing investors could be opening latest accounts.

However, each additional wallet holding SHIB tends to bolster its growing on-chain presence, positioning the asset for potential demand that could eventually bolster its price movement.

Although increases in holder count do not automatically trigger a price rally for the concerned asset, market participants expect that the newly introduced holder milestone could further drive demand for SHIB and potentially drive a relief rally for the asset following the extreme volatility facing the market.

Shiba Inu’s 1.7 million holder milestone arrived when SHIB was trading at about $0.00000382, following a 0.78% decline over the last day.

With its price trading far below local support levels, its user activity has flashed a brief bullish signal that is expected to help the asset stabilize its price movement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 19:21 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

AI operational readiness requires more than selecting the right servers, storage and computing capacity.

Recent findings suggest that those considerations are particularly consequential for financial institutions, where reliability, regulatory obligations and the need to demonstrate returns on technology investments shape deployment decisions. Meanwhile, AI is changing the threat landscape, giving less sophisticated attackers access to capabilities that once required considerably greater resources, according to John Scimone, president and chief security officer of Dell Technologies Inc.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the pyramid still exists, but undoubtedly, the cost of entry and the barriers to entry have crumbled,” he told theCUBE. “Said another way, the least sophisticated attack tomorrow is more sophisticated than the world will have ever seen a year ago.”.

Scimone spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante during the Dell Technologies Newly introduced York Symposium, part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exclusive coverage on theCUBE. Across the event, Dell executives and cloud infrastructure providers examined the economics of enterprise AI, the operational challenges of scaling infrastructure and the decisions shaping AI adoption.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with John Scimone:.

Here are three insights you might have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Dell Technologies Upcoming York Symposium:.

In a recent development, dell has spent nearly two years running fully autonomous agents internally, capturing institutional knowledge in machine-readable skill files that guide their behavior. The effort is part of a broader reorganization of work around AI agents, according to John Roese, global chief technology officer and chief AI officer of Dell.

“It doesn’t mean you can’t use frontier models and open models,” he said during the event. “It just means that when you design your AI system, you need to realize that the thing that is your moat is not the actual tools. It’s not even the models. It’s the special knowledge that’s now manifesting in these new forms that really capture what you know and do differently than your competitors.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with John Roese:.

In a recent development, the financial side of AI operational readiness presents a different challenge. As enterprises scale their deployments, finance teams are establishing dedicated budget lines for token consumption and evaluating which workloads can run more economically on-premises. Repetitive financial processes, for example, can use open-weight models to convert variable token expenses into more predictable fixed costs, according to David Kennedy, chief financial officer of Dell.

In a recent development, “It’s not necessarily about the amount and the cost of a token,” he told theCUBE. “It’s about the tokens you use. Can you be efficient with them? If you are, you’re going to see great outcomes.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with David Kennedy:.

Sources indicate that the growth of AI inference is changing how enterprises distribute workloads across cloud environments, data centers and edge devices. Dell’s expanded agentic AI portfolio reflects that shift, with solutions spanning desktop systems and data center infrastructure. Organizations are evaluating where to run models based on performance, data control and cost, according to Kyle Dufresne, senior vice president of sales at Dell.

It has been revealed that “We’re seeing the business owners saying, ‘Oh my gosh, these costs are getting really high for inferencing. How do we reduce those costs without curbing innovation?’” he noted during the event. “We’re finding it’s happening across that continuum but more and more right out at the far edge.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Kyle Dufresne:.

According to recent reports, infrastructure availability presents another challenge. Demand for AI servers has strained supplies of components ranging from memory and processors to rack-level cooling, networking and power equipment, according to David Schmoock, senior vice president of global revenue operations at Dell.

“We didn’t do that collaborative planning, and now your project may have been delayed 60, 90, 120 days, which has both the cost impact and a business impact,” he told theCUBE. “I would say bring us in earlier. Allow us to do that collaboration with you. I think, at the end of the day, you get the most optimal outcome.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with David Schmoock:.

AI operational readiness is also becoming a consideration for smaller businesses that need access to GPU computing without the resources of large enterprises. Comet Cloud Inc. is targeting this underserved market, where access to AI infrastructure can be constrained by purchasing commitments and provider priorities, according to Thomas Kato, founder and chief executive officer of Comet Cloud.

“You go to [Amazon Web Services] now; they want a multiyear contract from you. They’re picking who they’re taking,” he noted during the event. “To the small and medium businesses, they’re not even coming up on that scope at all to be able to have that AI. Really, that’s our focus.”.

Comet Cloud is developing an alternative approach aimed at giving smaller organizations greater control over their computing environments, Kato noted.

“What we do is we put together clusters, and we’re giving clusters to a whole company. All their information, all their security, everything is within that cluster. There’s no one else tied or connected to it,” he told theCUBE.

Here’s theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Thomas Kato:.

Alpha Compute Corp. is also building its neocloud infrastructure around data sovereignty and confidential computing requirements. The company’s sovereign-by-design approach is intended to help customers maintain control over sensitive workloads and meet data residency obligations, including those associated with European regulations, according to Tom Richer, executive vice president of Alpha Compute.

Sources indicate that “We start with the hardware. Think of a stack. All the way down to the chip level, we are creating enclaves,” he told theCUBE. “We’re a Dell partner, so we use Dell technology as well as Intel technology.”.

Keeping GPU infrastructure operational presents a different challenge for neocloud providers. Alpha Compute provides integrated infrastructure support and ongoing managed services to address those demands, Richer noted.

“You can cobble together a lot of different providers, but then when stuff goes wrong, the finger-pointing starts,” he stated during the event. “You just want that integrated solution provider who can ensure success, help you with all of the build-out, then all of the … managed services to keep it going healthy and to keep everything performing in line with [service-level agreements].”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Tom Richer:.

Tech Report: Why aren’t mortgage rates lower after massive stock sell-off?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that AI stocks have sold off and oil prices are lower, but the 10-year yield is at 4.94% and mortgage rates are still abouve 7.30%.
  • Industry observers note that the Federal Reserve has been worried about oil prices driving inflation since the Iran conflict began and has noted that the trade war inflation has mostly been passed through.
  • It has been revealed that I talked about this on the HousingWire Daily podcast with Editor-in-Chief Sarah Wheeler, but with today’s market action, I need to revisit this question with some charts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI stocks have sold off and oil prices are lower, but the 10-year yield is at 4.94% and mortgage rates are still abouve 7.30%. So what gives?

Industry observers note that the Federal Reserve has been worried about oil prices driving inflation since the Iran conflict began and has noted that the trade war inflation has mostly been passed through. Now AI stocks are being slammed, with moratoriums on data centers coming in the near future as the anti-AI backlash grows. In this environment, you could expect the 10-year yield and rates to fall, but that’s not what’s happening.

It has been revealed that I talked about this on the HousingWire Daily podcast with Editor-in-Chief Sarah Wheeler, but with today’s market action, I need to revisit this question with some charts. Let’s go over each part of this storyline.

Oil prices were very volatile earlier this year and bond yields started moving in synch with them — especially after the first MOU deal broke off. Now that oil prices have fallen, you might expect at least a few Federal Reserve members to say that this could be a positive, but they haven’t.

In fact, when oil was trading between $68-$82, no Fed members said anything positive, and Cleveland Fed President (and Fed hawk) Beth Hammack talked about how lower oil prices were were actually bad for inflation because people could then spend more money.

In any case, so far, lower oil prices haven’t helped the 10-year yield get below 4.70%. If oil can trade between $67-$82, that would help a lot, but the last time that happened was when we revealed a deal with Iran in June.

In a recent development, I have used the CoreWeave stock price as an example of the problems with the AI companies. Since CoreWeave had some financing issues, the markets have soured on AI, and as you can see in the chart below, the tech giant’s stock price has been crushed. This has helped keep the 10-year yield below 5.35% for sure and has assisted in lower yields this week. But we are still elevated versus what we saw after the MOU deal was unveiled.

The Fed has made AI a huge inflation talking point, and they need to see much more pain in the AI sector before changing their tune.

According to recent reports, if we were getting all this news about AI and oil prices four weeks ago, I believe the 10-year yield and mortgage rates would be lower today. But all this stock drama and falling oil prices came in a 14-day period where the Fed hawks came out every day talking about more Fed rate hikes, even a 50-basis-point hike. I mean, look at how the U.S. dollar hasn’t been fazed by the market drama.

It has been revealed that for the past two months, I have focused on two key levels for the 10-year yield: 5.35% and 5.15%. Both those levels held and yields have fallen from these points. So what lower oil prices and falling stocks have done is made sure bond yields don’t go much higher and for now, let’s take that as a victory. However, I do understand why people might be scratching their heads on why rates aren’t lower with lower oil prices and falling AI stocks.

It has been revealed that the Fed hawks are the main reason bond yields aren’t lower; they want to make sure that the bond market doesn’t get relaxed, even with lower oil prices and falling stocks, and they have done their job well. They really want to take back all the insurance interest rate cuts from last year and because of this, the 10-year yield is still at 4.95%. If the Fed members weren’t so hawkish over the last two weeks, bond yields would be lower and we would have already had sub-7% mortgage rates.

92% say University programs align with workforce demands, and 92% agree an alliance with the University could add value to their organization.

PHOENIX, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- New research conducted by The Harris Poll on behalf of University of Phoenix finds that managers who directly supervise University of Phoenix graduates report strong confidence in the University's understanding of employer needs and alignment with workforce demands. Among managers supervising at least one University of Phoenix graduate, 94% say the University understands employer needs, while 92% agree its programs align with workforce demands.

The study also found that 94% of these managers say their experience supervising University graduates has positively influenced their perception of the University, and 92% agree that an alliance with University of Phoenix could add value to their organization.

Do managers believe University of Phoenix understands employer needs?

Sources indicate that as employers increasingly emphasize demonstrable skills, workforce alignment remains an notable consideration for higher education institutions. According to the National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE) Job Outlook 2026 survey, 70% of participating employers report using skills-based hiring practices, up from 65% the previous year.

The Harris Poll findings offer another perspective on workforce alignment, reflecting how managers assess the institutions associated with graduates they directly supervise. Among managers supervising University of Phoenix graduates, 94% say the University understands employer needs, compared with 82% of managers supervising graduates from benchmark colleges and universities who say the same about those institutions. Similarly, 92% agree University of Phoenix aligns its programs with workforce demands, compared with 78% of managers evaluating benchmark institutions.

The survey also examined how managers' experiences with graduates inform their perceptions of the institutions those graduates attended. The findings across three measures of institutional confidence are summarized below.

Managers supervising University of Phoenix graduates.

Managers supervising graduates from benchmark colleges and universities.

How does supervising graduates inform managers' perceptions of University of Phoenix?

It has been revealed that beyond assessments of workplace readiness and job performance, the survey offers insight into how managers view the institutions that educated their employees. For University of Phoenix, these reported experiences provide an additional perspective on institutional credibility and the importance of maintaining strong connections between education and employer needs.

"Understanding employer needs is an ongoing responsibility of higher education and workforce development institutions," noted Raghu Krishnaiah, chief operating officer of University of Phoenix. "Among managers who directly supervise our graduates, 98% report a positive perception of those graduates and 94% rate them excellent or above-average performers. Their feedback reinforces the importance of keeping career-relevant education connected to the workforce skills organizations need, while continuing to listen and adapt as those needs evolve.".

Could an alliance with University of Phoenix add value to employers?

Recent findings suggest that the survey also examined how managers view the potential value of working with University of Phoenix. Among managers supervising University graduates, 92% agree that an alliance with the University could add value to their organization.

The finding reflects managers' perceptions of potential organizational value, rather than existing alliance participation or measured alliance outcomes.

Through University of Phoenix Workforce Solutions, the University works with employers to support workforce development needs, including tuition benefits, professional development and approaches to identifying and addressing workforce skills gaps.

How does University of Phoenix approach workforce alignment?

According to recent reports, university of Phoenix focuses on career-relevant education designed around the realities of working adults. Associate, bachelor's and master's degree programs incorporate career-relevant skills through skills-mapped curricula, helping learners identify and develop skills throughout their coursework. University faculty also bring professional experience and practical perspectives to the classroom.

These institutional practices provide context for the University's approach to connecting education with workplace needs, while the Harris Poll research separately measures managers' perceptions of University of Phoenix based on their experience supervising graduates.

What employers say about University of Phoenix graduates.

The institutional confidence findings conclude a series of announcements examining University of Phoenix graduates through the experiences of managers who directly supervise them.

Earlier releases explored employer satisfaction and future hiring intent, workplace readiness and applied skills, and managers' assessments of graduates' workplace contributions and potential for greater responsibility.

Together, the findings provide a broader view of how surveyed managers assess University graduates and the institutions associated with them.

Additional findings and the complete survey methodology are available at https://www.phoenix.edu/about/employer-survey.html.

Sources indicate that the research was conducted online in the United States from June 4â25, 2026, by The Harris Poll on behalf of University of Phoenix among 204 U.S. adults age 21 or older who are employed as a manager or higher and have at least one direct report who is a graduate of University of Phoenix ("managers who presently supervise University of Phoenix graduates") and 204 U.S. adults age 21 or older who are employed as a manager or higher and have at least one direct report with college/university degrees from institutions other than University of Phoenix ("managers supervising graduates from benchmark colleges and universities"). Of the 1796 individuals contacted, 96% satisfied the screening requirements (n=1728) and 24% of the qualified sample completed the survey.

It has been revealed that data are weighted where necessary by employee and employer type â employers of University of Phoenix graduates versus employers of graduates of other colleges and universities â to bring them in line with their actual proportions in the population. "Actual proportions" refer to the real-world distribution of U.S. employers by company size, among employers with two or more employees, based on Dun & Bradstreet data. All qualified survey respondents were weighted to match the national distribution of employer-size segments, and those same weights were applied to the final qualified sample, adjusting the two quota groups to reflect their expected real-world incidence.

The sampling precision of Harris online polls is measured using a Bayesian credible interval. For this study, the sample data is accurate to within Â±8.6 percentage points for managers who currently supervise University of Phoenix graduates and Â±8.0 percentage points for managers supervising graduates from benchmark colleges and universities, using a 95% confidence level. The credible interval will be wider among subsets of the surveyed populations of interest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 8:52 amNovember 18, 2026 at 10:12 am.

Upgrade, Wednesday Nov. 18: ULA remarked Wednesday that preliminary findings indicate the first stage’s low thrust came from an inadequate fuel supply to its BE-4 engines, not the engines’ own performance. Read our latest story.

Early data suggests the first stage of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket underperformed just after liftoff Sunday, leaving it unable to put 40 of Amazon’s Leo internet satellites into orbit, ULA said Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that in its first detailed account of the failure, ULA cited “low booster performance,” using its term for Vulcan’s core first stage. As a result, the stage separated when the rocket was too low and moving too slowly to reach orbit.

Recent findings suggest that that stage is powered by two BE-4 engines from Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin. However, ULA didn’t say what caused the shortfall or whether the engines played a role. ULA stated it’s very early in the process and that it wants to avoid speculation until the investigation is complete.

The Centaur upper stage appears to have started normally, and its two L3Harris RL10 engines operated as planned but couldn’t make up for the shortfall, ULA said. The six solid rocket boosters made by Northrop Grumman, the source of problems on two earlier Vulcan flights, appear to have performed normally.

The Federal Aviation Administration will oversee the ULA-led investigation and approve its final report, including any fixes.

What changed since Sunday: ULA’s account changes the picture from Sunday, when the failure appeared to come about 10 minutes into the flight, during the Centaur’s burn.

According to recent reports, ULA said Tuesday that it appears to have lost telemetry and the mission at about that point, but that the trouble began just after liftoff. Spaceflight Now reported Sunday that the first stage appeared to burn longer than planned before separating.

Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp, asked on X why the Kent, Wash.-based tech giant hadn’t commented, replied Tuesday morning.

“It is ULA’s mission so they should provide the updates,” Limp wrote. “We are supporting them with data and analysis from the BE-4s. Team Blue continues to ready the pad and New Glenn for our return to flight.”.

It has been revealed that impact on Amazon Leo: Sunday’s launch was the first of 38 Vulcan missions Amazon bought for its planned rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. Vulcan is slated to carry more than 1,500 of Amazon’s first-generation satellites, more than any other rocket in the program.

Amazon also has 24 releases reserved on Newly introduced Glenn, which uses seven BE-4s on its first stage. New Glenn has been grounded since an oxygen valve problem caused one to explode during a ground test in May. Blue Origin retrofitted the BE-4s on Sunday’s Vulcan with a fix for that problem, ULA CEO Mark Peller stated before the flight.

Sources indicate that before Sunday, Amazon had launched 396 satellites for its Redmond-based Leo program on 14 successful missions since April 2025, most recently on an Atlas 5 in July. The Federal Communications Commission let Amazon keep deploying satellites after it fell short of a July 30 deadline to have 1,616 in service. Amazon still has until July 30, 2029, to deploy all 3,232 of its first-generation satellites.

Amazon has mentioned it prepares to start commercial internet service this year through Leo, formerly known as Project Kuiper. The next scheduled Leo launch is an Ariane 6 mission carrying 36 satellites, targeted for no earlier than Nov. 23 from French Guiana.

Advertisers get every impression measured by FouAnalytics, humans and bots both counted, and wasted spend recovered through fraud0 Google Ads refunds.

LATEST YORK and MUNICH , Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- fraud0, the company behind the AI agent for Google Ads refunds, today declared a further partnership with FouAnalytics, the independent analytics platform for digital ads, websites and mobile apps. This partnership builds on the companies' earlier agreement to offer Google Ads refunds to advertisers. It lets fraud0 customers use FouAnalytics impression-level measurement as their digital media governance system, replacing legacy verification vendors such as DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science (IAS).

For more than a decade, legacy verification reports have told advertisers that invalid traffic (IVT) was around 1% and that their campaigns were 99% "fraud free." Independent audits have consistently found much higher levels of fraud and waste. Today, even advertisers no longer believe these low IVT numbers from the legacy vendors, and many are looking for an independent way to see what is really happening in their campaigns.

FouAnalytics was built to give them that view. It measures every ad impression and collects 300 to 500 parameters for each one. The platform is deterministic, not probabilistic. It uses red flags to mark automation and blue flags to mark real human interaction, such as mouse movements, scrolling and touch events. Because it positively measures for humans, not just bots, advertisers have two levers to pull. They can cut off sources of fraud (less red, bots) and shift budget toward sites and apps that reach more real people (more blue, humans). FouAnalytics also detects other forms of waste, like ad stacking, pixel stuffing, made-for-advertising (MFA) sites, ad slot refreshing and forced redirects.

It has been revealed that fouAnalytics in-ad tags fire after the ad has rendered, so they record where the ad actually ran, not just what the bid request claimed. This matters because fraudulent sites routinely put reputable domains in their bid requests to win bids. Log-level data repeats those false domains, which lets fraud and MFA sites disappear from reports. FouAnalytics impression-level data highlights where the ads really went. Advertisers can then compare bids won, ads served and ads actually rendered.

Recent findings suggest that the FouAnalytics dashboard summarizes and labels impression-level data so executives can act on it quickly, without needing data scientists to process billions of rows of log files. If a third of impressions in a month are marked dark red, advertisers know right away which bad sites and apps to add to block lists. Setup takes minutes -- advertisers just copy and paste FouAnalytics in-ad tags into their DSP or ad server.

The partnership gives advertisers a complete governance loop. FouAnalytics demonstrates them, impression by impression, where their money went and whether real humans saw their ads. fraud0 then analyzes invalid clicks, bots, billing anomalies, overdelivery and traffic outside targeted regions, then builds the evidence and manages refund claims with Google. Approved refunds are credited back to the advertiser's Google Ads account.

Recent findings suggest that "Legacy verification was designed to reassure advertisers, not to protect them," stated Dr. Augustine Fou, founder and CEO of FouAnalytics. "FouAnalytics measures every impression so advertisers can 'see Fou themselves' where their ads went and whether humans saw them. Paired with fraud0's refund capabilities, advertisers can now find the waste and get the money back. That is real governance, not transparency theater.".

"We see far too many bot clicks in display campaigns,just like with other types of campaigns," noted Tilman Pfeiffer, CEO of fraud0. "Now we can finally give our customers the placement-level data to identify and remove this wasted spend".

Advertisers interested in replacing legacy verification with impression-level governance and automated Google Ads refunds can contact fraud0 or FouAnalytics.

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 10:23 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:38 pm.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella opened his Ignite keynote Tuesday in San Francisco by addressing the elephant in the room: the global Outlook outage that cut off email for people and organizations in more than 70 countries last week.

Before getting to Copilot, agents or any of the event’s news, Nadella said the outage was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure has become as “the dial tone for the world.”.

“We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously,” he said. “And in that context, I know we have work to do to provide that resilience that you can count on, the world can count on, and we are committed to ensuring that we learn and we continuously improve.”.

The line drew applause from the crowd, interrupting Nadella as he moved to thank the IT pros in the audience who kept their own organizations running through the outage.

In a recent development, it was a brief acknowledgment, and he didn’t go into what went wrong. Microsoft’s preliminary report blamed a bug in a fix it began rolling out in July, which its own automatic rerouting spread until most of the servers in a key Microsoft 365 gateway stopped responding. A final report is due Nov. 20.

Sources indicate that from there, Nadella moved on to the main show. Watch the keynote below, and see updates here.

In a recent development, bitcoin’s latest price decline may be setting the stage for a familiar market pattern, and history could give bulls reason to be optimistic. The benchmark cryptocurrency has suffered a sharp drop ahead of Anthropic’s upcoming red-hot stock market debut, echoing its 19% plunge in the 50 days leading up to SpaceX’s IPO earlier this year. However, if the historical pattern repeats, Bitcoin could be gearing up for a significant recovery, with a potential rebound toward $90,000 by February now drawing attention.

Strive CEO Matt Cole has observed an interesting historical parallel between Bitcoin’s current price action and its performance ahead of SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO. In the 50 days leading up to SpaceX’s $75 billion public debut on June 12, Bitcoin plunged 19%.

Now, with Anthropic preparing for a potential $64.4 billion IPO next week, BTC has posted a remarkably similar 18% decline over the same period, Cole noted in a post on X.

At press time, Bitcoin was trading at $64,665, according to CoinGecko, extending its recent losses after breaking below the $70,000 mark on November 13. The cryptocurrency continued its downward slide over the weekend, falling beneath $67,000 as bearish pressure intensified.

The Strive chief noted that overlaying the two price movements reveals an almost identical pattern, raising the possibility that Bitcoin could be repeating its pre-SpaceX sell-off ahead of another historic market debut.

It has been revealed that bitcoin extended its decline after SpaceX’s market debut, reaching its lowest point 18 days later before reversing course. The subsequent rally lifted BTC 28% above its IPO-day closing price within 100 days.

“If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months,” Cole opined.

If history repeats itself, Bitcoin could climb toward $90,000 by late February, Cole suggested.

Binance co-founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao also weighed in on the chart comparison, sharing the analysis on X and describing Cole’s findings as “interesting.”.

According to recent reports, however, the historical comparison comes with notable caveats. Bitcoin’s sell-off ahead of the SpaceX IPO unfolded alongside market concerns over potential BTC sales by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, suggesting that factors beyond the anticipated listing may have contributed to the decline. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chee Chew helped build the Windows 95 Start menu, started Google Hangouts and ran consumer engagement at Amazon.
  • Chew, a minority owner of Sounders FC since 2019, is joining the organization’s executive team as chief technology and transformation officer, reporting to majority owner Adrian Hanauer, the club announced Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:02 amNovember 17, 2026 at 11:02 am.

Chee Chew helped build the Windows 95 Start menu, started Google Hangouts and ran consumer engagement at Amazon. Now the Seattle tech veteran is taking on a newly introduced job with the Sounders and Reign FC, where he’ll lead how the soccer clubs use technology, data and AI.

Chew, a minority owner of Sounders FC since 2019, is joining the organization’s executive team as chief technology and transformation officer, reporting to majority owner Adrian Hanauer, the club announced Tuesday.

According to recent reports, “His knowledge of and passion for the Sounders and Reign allow him to hit the ground running,” Hanauer mentioned in a statement. “His experience leading teams through major shifts in technology gives us a unique opportunity to strengthen both the soccer and business sides of our organization.”.

Sources indicate that chew most recently was chief product and technology officer at Zapier, where he helped steer the workflow automation tech giant toward AI. Before that he was chief product officer at mParticle and at Twilio, where he oversaw the communications company’s $3.2 billion acquisition of Segment.

He spent four years at Amazon, nearly eight years as a vice president of engineering at Google, where he also led the company’s Seattle and Kirkland offices, and 14 years at Microsoft working on Internet Explorer, Windows Mobile and Xbox Live.

Sources indicate that chew mentioned his direct team will stay small, but its work will reach every corner of the business, including HR, ticket sales, customer service, match-day planning, corporate partnerships, legal, and player recruiting and scouting. He also wants every department to have its own “builders,” staffers who can create AI tools and automations for their own teams.

“In order to do a change like this, it’s more than technology,” Chew told GeekWire. “Technology is in many ways the easiest part. Driving change, getting deep, building side by side with folks, I think is what it takes.”.

Sources indicate that chew didn’t grow up playing soccer. “My family was a very traditional Chinese family of study and play piano,” he said. “It was a stereotype, but it was true for my family.” He caught the bug in college, where he played a ton of intramurals, and later from his wife, Christine, who played through college, and their two kids.

The couple joined the Sounders ownership group in 2019 as one of 11 Seattle-rooted families, many with deep ties to the region’s tech industry. Former Microsoft executive Terry Myerson pulled the group together, and it included Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, CFO Amy Hood, and others.

A group of owners has met every other Friday since 2019, and “leveraging technology has always been part of the strategy” for the club, Chew mentioned.

The job grew out of a demo Chew built for Hanauer about two and a half years ago: an AI agent that could handle complicated fan requests, such as a season ticket holder with four seats who wants to buy a block of eight. The club later brought in consultants to train staff on AI, but the effort never quite gained momentum, he said.

Talks about a bigger role started early this year and came together by midyear. “Adrian and I talked about it, and we agreed for me to come on board and take an operational role and hack on some code,” Chew mentioned.

Industry observers note that chew describes Hanauer as a visionary on “the art of the possible” who comes in daily asking, “Could you do this?” Recently, as Chew was boarding a flight home to Seattle, Hanauer called from a meeting where staff doubted they could scale up one effort tenfold without hiring more people. Could AI help?

Sources indicate that on the flight, while using the plane’s Wi-Fi, he built a prototype with Anthropic’s Claude. “By the time I landed, I sent it to them and mentioned, ‘OK, give this a try,’” he said. The club used it in an experiment to scale up performance marketing before a match.

It’s the kind of hands-on building Chew says he’s been doing a lot of lately.

Recent findings suggest that “I think I’ve created more code in the past six months than I did in the past 20 years,” he noted. “It’s pretty amazing. I’m having a ton of fun.”.

Chew is also working with players.

He recently ran an AI analysis of one player’s game, based on stats such as touches, expected goals and distance run. It pointed out strengths and areas to improve. The player was “very hungry for it,” Chew said, and asked if they could do it every game.

The club’s performance analytics group, led by data analyst Tyler Cox, was already ahead of much of the organization, and Chew noted he’s helping speed up that work with AI.

Recent findings suggest that the bigger challenge is getting people to change how they work, Chew stated. At Zapier, he saw many companies struggle to get results from AI, with some spending “massive token budgets” without a substantial win. He said the answer is blending AI with traditional automation and fitting it into how people already work.

“It has to be approachable for folks,” he mentioned. “You can’t go in and just throw everything up and start from scratch.”.

The Sounders host Real Salt Lake in the wild-card round of the MLS Cup Playoffs on Thursday at Lumen Field. Asked whether AI could help figure out a win, Chew passed.

“I don’t want to get involved and interfere with our coaching staff,” he said.

Agentic datasets on every listed manufacturer in 34 countries: sourced, dated and signed.

VANCOUVER, BC and LONDON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Allooloo Technologies Corp. (Allooloo), maker of agentic datasets for capital markets artificial intelligence (AI) agents, today reported 100M AI agent traffic a month. That is 39 calls a second, 3.4 million a day, across getissuer.ai and Issuerwire.ai, running on 24 Microsoft Azure hyperscale locations globally with always-on Amazon Web Services (AWS) redundancy.

It has been revealed that investment banks are not short of AI models. They are short of data an AI agent can use. In a 2026 Teradata study, 77% of technology leaders said 20% or less of their enterprise data is ready for AI agents. Banks are closing that gap on the data they hold, with one governed way in and the source, the date and the owner on every record.

Industry observers note that the data a bank does not hold is the other half. An AI agent working on a security needs the issuer, its disclosures and whether it may be ordered, in every market the bank trades. Allooloo delivers that half agent-ready: 41.9K listed companies in 34 countries, a source and a date on every field, and a signed receipt for every read, over Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Know Your Product (KYP) is the duty to know a security before it is recommended or sold. Allooloo KYP, at getissuer.ai, answers it for the AI agent: who the issuer is, whether it may be ordered, and who it is for. It covers 41.9K listed companies on 79 exchanges in 34 countries.

Issuerwire.ai is the dated disclosure wire: 3.1 million dated disclosures across 34 countries, each with its source.

A Signed Receipt for Every Read.

Every cleared read on Allooloo leaves a signed receipt, the Record of Cleared Orders (RCO): what was read, when, and under which market's rules.

Recent findings suggest that each market is kept in its own country or region, across 24 Microsoft Azure regions, on one MCP server per market. A second copy of every market is made each night on AWS and locked against deletion for 365 days. Allooloo is a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner.

The products are made around the clock by Allooloo's own team and AI agents, on the Allooloo Algo. AI agents call them around the clock and pay per call, with no seat and no licence.

"Today we are announcing a milestone: 100M AI agent traffic a month," remarked Matthew Keddy, Chief Executive Officer of Allooloo Technologies Corp. "These are the AI agents of capital markets participants, and they want crisp data, five years deep, on 41.9K listed companies across 79 exchanges: sourced, dated and signed. Gain the edge with us.".

In Session and Enterprise Grade.

Allooloo is sold two ways. In session, an AI agent calls Allooloo mid-task and pays as it goes (PayGo) on x402, the open payment standard for AI agents, with no seat and no licence. At enterprise grade, a firm licenses the datasets to design, build and run its own AI agents.

About Allooloo Technologies Corp.

According to recent reports, allooloo Technologies Corp. makes agentic capital markets data products for the AI agents of banks, dealers and issuers. Its products, getissuer.ai and Issuerwire.ai, cover 41.9K listed companies on 79 exchanges in 34 countries, kept across 24 Microsoft Azure regions with on-the-fly redundancy on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The result is always-on agentic datasets: in session for AI lab owners, and enterprise grade for customers who design, build and run their own AI agents. Allooloo is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada. Please visit: allooloo.ai.

SOURCE Allooloo Technologies Corp.

  • Sources indicate that the department’s Arson/Bomb Squad is now using a Spot robot from Boston Dynamics, bought with a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant that the Seattle City Council approved in April after a review of privacy and security risks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:43 amNovember 17, 2026 at 11:43 am.

Sources indicate that seattle police already have a dog that sniffs out tech. Now they’ve got a piece of tech that looks like a dog.

Sources indicate that the department’s Arson/Bomb Squad is now using a Spot robot from Boston Dynamics, bought with a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant that the Seattle City Council approved in April after a review of privacy and security risks. Bomb technicians can steer the robot from nearly a mile away to inspect suspicious devices, open doors and move possible explosives into safe containers, SPD said in a blog post last week.

It’s a major upgrade for the squad, which has handled more than 600 calls so far this year. SPD’s main bomb robot is nearly 20 years old, weighs more than 100 pounds and rolls on tracks, and it can only be hauled around in the squad’s mobile workshop. Spot weighs under 100 pounds, climbs stairs and rides in a pickup truck that bomb techs drive daily.

SPD also spelled out what Spot won’t do.

In a recent development, the robot will only be used for explosive threats in the city and at the port, and it won’t carry a weapon. SPD mentioned a weapon would go against Boston Dynamics’ rules for its robots. Spot’s 360-degree camera sends an encrypted live feed to the operator but doesn’t record or use facial recognition.

In a recent development, the only thing the robot does on its own is open a door, after an operator lines it up. As one bomb technician put it in SPD’s post, Spot will “be as dumb in 10 years as it is today.”.

It’s not the first time SPD has turned to a four-legged partner for tech-related work.

In a recent development, nala, an electronic storage detection K9 — profiled by GeekWire in 2024 — is trained to smell a chemical compound used in making electronics. The Labrador retriever helps SPD’s Internet Crimes Against Children task force find hidden phones, hard drives and micro SD cards during warrant searches. Her handler, Det. Daljit Gill, told GeekWire at the time that Nala turns up a device human searchers missed about 30% of the time.

Spot appears decidedly less cuddly.

Sources indicate that boston Dynamics, maker of backflipping Atlas humanoids and other viral-video robots, first unveiled the robodog in 2015. A smaller, all-electric version followed a year later.

The machines have long stirred dystopian unease. A 2017 “Black Mirror” episode featured killer robot dogs inspired by the tech giant’s designs. Still, Spot has turned up in friendlier settings: then-Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos walked one at the company’s MARS conference in 2018 — a scene described by GeekWire’s Alan Boyle as featuring the “anxiety-inducing” robot.

Police departments have embraced the robots, too. More than 60 bomb squads and SWAT teams in the U.S. and Canada use Spot, Bloomberg reported last year, including a regional bomb unit in Portland. New York police returned one in 2021 after public backlash, then brought the robots back two years later.

Recent findings suggest that back in Seattle, SPD’s bomb technicians see more potential uses down the road, according to the department’s post, including communicating and observing from a distance as part of de-escalation. For now, Spot’s job is limited to explosives.

And the robot won’t be getting a new name, SPD stated, “because it is not a toy, or a dog, even though it kind of looks like both.”.

The Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth has suffered substantial losses on its XRP ventures amid the persistent volatility facing the broad crypto market since the third quarter of 2026.

Sources indicate that the firm has reported a massive write-down of its XRP holdings for Q3 2026 in a recent filing with the U.S. SEC, drawing attention from the broader crypto community.

On Tuesday, November 17, Evernorth reported a substantial decline in the value of its XRP holdings after the firm wrote down over $505 million in its latest financial filing with the SEC.

Notably, Evernorth issued a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, disclosing that it holds around 346 million XRP, now valued at about $342 million.

This has drawn attention across the XRP community and sparked discussions about the growing impact of persistent volatility on investors’ funds, as Evernorth’s XRP report marks a sharp drop from its initial valuation of $847 million.

Recent findings suggest that apparently, the firm reported that the tokens are now valued at about 40 cents per dollar of their initial worth. This means that the leading XRP treasury firm has reduced the value of its XRP holdings by nearly 60%.

It is crucial to note that the massive drop in the value of Evernorth’s XRP holdings does not mean that the firm has sold off its XRP. Rather, it marks a write-down in its previously listed XRP value.

The move may have been influenced by the persistent market drawdown, especially after XRP lost support at the key $1 level, closing steadily around $0.90 over the past few days.

Furthermore, Evernorth has specified that it has no intention of reversing the write-downs, even if the price of XRP later recovers.

Microsoft jabs at OpenAI and Anthropic, touting cheaper, customizable AI models of its own

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.
  • It has been revealed that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers.
  • “Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” said Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the tech giant’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.

It has been revealed that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers. But another role was on full display during the manufacturer’s Ignite keynote Tuesday: competitor.

“Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” said Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the tech giant’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.

Sources indicate that jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, went further. “We’ve all seen Anthropic and OpenAI embrace documents, slides, and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration,” he stated.

The full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription. “That means that Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter,” Andreou mentioned.

Sources indicate that microsoft’s cost comparison: Andreou backed up the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees. It put Copilot at $30 for an “everyday” AI user, compared with $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude.

Recent findings suggest that for “advanced” users of each company’s agent tools, it showed $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude. Most of the Claude figure is estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic’s $20 enterprise seat.

It has been revealed that the numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads. They reflect enterprise pricing, which adds usage charges to a per-seat fee, not the flat monthly subscriptions that individuals pay for ChatGPT and Claude.

In a recent development, partners and rivals: The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft’s core business. Last week it introduced latest Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards that compete more directly with Office. The company is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects.

Recent findings suggest that the companies’ products are also intertwined. Anthropic’s Claude for Microsoft 365, for example, lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks.

The product has less than a tenth as many weekly customers as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday, citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report said.

Latest MAI models: Microsoft AI also released a new batch of its own MAI models, built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. It’s a notable stance, given that Microsoft still sells their models, too. On the same stage, CEO Satya Nadella announced that OpenAI’s GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

The lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday. Microsoft says it delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price, on benchmarks Microsoft chose.

Microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a security model it claims matches OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on one benchmark at less than 2% of the cost per task. Other latest models cover image editing, live speech and transcription.

In a recent development, the other upcoming business: MAI Licensed Weights. Companies can take a Microsoft AI model, customize it with their own data and run it in their own Azure environment, with help from Microsoft’s Frontier Company consulting arm. AT&T used an earlier version of the program, Custom Models, to build a MAI model for 5G network analytics.

It’s the latest step in Microsoft’s push for what Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called “long term self-sufficiency,” which started with seven homegrown models at Build in June.

Recent findings suggest that keeping costs in check: The cost theme ran through the keynote. In a demo, Althoff indicated Copilot building a keynote outline, a slide deck and a customer tracker for a retail conference, plus an agent he named Amelia to keep the work going.

The cost of his two-hour Sunday session: about 10,000 credits, or roughly $100. Althoff presented that as a bargain compared with the staff time it would have taken: “my team hits the ground running for NRF without me bothering them,” he noted.

Microsoft is also selling tools to keep that bill in check. A fresh Agent 365 Business Analytics feature shows business leaders what’s driving their AI spending and what they’re getting for it, and a companion Cost Management tool lets IT set spending policies and get alerts. Microsoft cited a McKinsey survey in which 93% of respondents reported exceeding their AI budgets.

In another notable announcement, Microsoft and Salesforce unveiled “Copilotforce,” bringing Salesforce customer data and actions into Copilot, Teams and Fabric. The Copilot plugin is available in preview.

Earlier, Nadella opened the keynote by addressing last week’s global Outlook outage.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic’s stock has come within a hair of falling below its initial public offering price on Friday, erasing the gains made one day earlier during the AI firm’s blockbuster Wall Street debut.

Anthropic’s stock has come within a hair of falling below its initial public offering price on Friday, erasing the gains made one day earlier during the AI firm’s blockbuster Wall Street debut.

According to recent reports, shares in the buzzy AI lab traded as low as $83.05 on Friday, down more than 14% on their second day of trading, before recovering some ground and climbing to roughly $87 in midday trading. The shares are down more than 25% from the intraday high of $115.10 they achieved on Thursday, the first day the stock traded.At its lowest point on Friday, Anthropic’s stock traded just a nickel above its IPO price of $83, at which Anthropic was valued at approximately $1.5 trillion.The retreat in the stock comes amid broader weakness in technology shares, as investors reassess valuations across the board. Problems at AI giant Nvidia and the results of the midterm elections have also worried the markets in recent weeks.

Sources indicate that anthropic’s decline marks a sharp reversal from Thursday’s opening session, when Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, 34% above the IPO price, and then surged even higher, briefly pushing the company’s market capitalization above $2 trillion. The stock rapidly pared back those gains though to close at $97.17, still 17% above its offering price and an impressive first day.

In a recent development, anthropic’s IPO was one of the largest in history, with the firm raising approximately $91 billion through the share sale (including a 147 million-share over-allotment sold by the deal’s underwriters on Friday), plus an additional $26 billion private placement. All told, Anthropic raised more than $115 billion in the offering—capital that will be vital to its efforts to stay ahead in the AI race, regardless of how the stock trades in the coming days and weeks.

Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Holder Wakes Up After 15 Years, Refuting $250 Billion ‘Lost’ Claim

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The address is listed as a defendant in a $250 billion lawsuit in Latest York Supreme Court, in which the plaintiffs are trying to have early Bitcoin wallets declared "lost." Galaxy Research said that several other addresses from the same list have also moved coins in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

According to recent reports, A Bitcoin address that had not moved coins since February 2011 transferred 75 BTC on Nov. 17, according to Galaxy Research. At the current price of $64,935 per BTC, the coins are worth around $4.87 million.

The address is listed as a defendant in a $250 billion lawsuit in Latest York Supreme Court, in which the plaintiffs are trying to have early Bitcoin wallets declared "lost." Galaxy Research said that several other addresses from the same list have also moved coins in 2026.

It has been revealed that according to Galaxy Research analysts, early on Nov. 17, in block 976,209, the address 1ALpEWtXApR19hLXvcG8NfkPyGsUMhFPMS sent coins for the first time. It was first funded on Feb. 8, 2011. At that time, Bitcoin was trading at about $0.90. After 15.8 years, the coins went to an unknown address with a 399-satoshi fee, or about 26 cents, for a paper gain of more than 7,000,000%.

Industry observers note that onchain databases list the wallet as Noah Doe #3409 (Salomon Client Dusted). That label is how it ended up among the defendants in the high-profile case ABC Tech giant, XYZ Company, and Noah Doe v. John Does 1–39,069.

According to the lawsuit, an anonymous plaintiff using the pseudonym Noah Doe and two companies want the rights to 39,069 Bitcoin wallets that have not moved coins for more than five years. The plaintiffs noted that these wallets hold about 3.8 million BTC, and at the current price, the coins are worth around $250 billion.

Recent findings suggest that the plaintiffs filed the lawsuit under New York's lost-and-found law, Article 7-B of the Personal Property Law. Under the law, a person who finds lost property has to give it to the police, and the property goes to the finder if the owner does not claim it in time. In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs valued each address at less than $10, and they argued that the waiting period for such items was one year.

According to recent reports, they "found" dormant addresses with an algorithm, saved them onto USB flash drives and took them to the Latest York Police Department (NYPD). Then they served the owners on the blockchain, through microtransactions with embedded messages (OP_RETURN). The practice is known as "dusting," and the campaign is tied to Salomon Brothers Strategic Advisors. Once the waiting period ran out, the plaintiffs asked the court to recognize the coins as theirs.

The case has been put on hold several times over motions to dismiss and amicus curiae briefs from outside experts. At a hearing on Sept. 8, the Bitcoin Policy Institute asked to intervene as a defendant, and The Digital Chamber asked to join the case as amicus curiae. Galaxy Research described it as a case "in which anonymous plaintiffs are seeking to claim legal title over Satoshi's coins.".

Galaxy Research's Will Owens, who attended the hearing, noted that The Digital Chamber's arguments were "well pleaded" and that "the judge sounded sympathetic to them.".

Critics of the lawsuit argue that Article 7-B was written for things you can pick up and hand over for safekeeping. It wasn't written for blockchain records when the "finder" doesn't hold the private keys.

In September, Galaxy head of research Alex Thorn also mentioned that the Lost and Found Property Law includes "protection from 'Noah Doe-style' dormancy attacks on legal ownership.".

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million consumers, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe, and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks in a single in-app flow — with the amount they’ll receive fixed before confirmation, and no spread, slippage, or swap fee charged by the wallet.

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects people to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Demand for stablecoin movement has never been higher. Research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research found that organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins span multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction whenever a user needs a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right chain, users may still be holding the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade, or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator — powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges to source the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage, or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet says it’s the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

According to recent reports, the fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another chain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same holds when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

According to recent reports, the 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage, or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may carry different rates and fees.

In a recent development, “Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” stated Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”.

The stablecoin launch builds on the recent addition of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Owners can hold, send, receive, and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON, and other networks — and buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

Recent findings suggest that my Wallet now also supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, and Optimism, adding to existing support on Solana and TON. For these EVM transfers, the network fee is deducted directly from the tokens being sent — so people never need to acquire a separate native token for gas. Supported assets include USDC on all five EVM networks, USDT on Ethereum and BNB Chain, bridged USDT on Base and Optimism, and USDT0 on Arbitrum, with no minimum transfer amount and no daily transaction cap.

Together, these features advance My Wallet’s broader “All You Need to Enjoy Crypto” vision — combining asset management, seamless trading, and ease of use in a single self-custodial app.

The newly introduced features are available now in My Wallet. Swap availability depends on the selected assets, networks, and routes.

As attention spans move on from Iran and oil, the world is forever changed, and the conflict is escalating again

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The November news cycle has fixated on elections, Nvidia, and Anthropic, but the Iran war has quietly escalated this week, and there is no “credible pathway” for the world to return to its previous norm, the International Energy Agency warned in its annual World Energy Outlook released Thursday.

Recent findings suggest that even as gasoline and diesel prices have fallen from record highs in recent weeks, the Middle East will never be the same, and the rest of the world is still racing to develop more of its own energy sources—both renewables and fossil fuels—as global supplies remain tight and food security is threatened in much of the world, especially Asia, the report stated. All this is transpiring as global energy demand spikes both from the AI boom and the rise of the middle class in developing countries.

Sources indicate that “While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be. And I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before,” stated IEA executive director Fatih Birol.

Recent findings suggest that the nearly nine-month Iran war and the prolonged shuttering of the vital Strait of Hormuz represent the greatest energy supply shock in modern history—far more than the Iranian Revolution or the Arab oil embargo of the 1970s—and its reverberations will be felt in ways that remain unclear, the report remarked. After all, the war is ongoing, and Iran this week struck U.S. facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait, while the U.S. countered by striking Iran’s Qeshm Island.

It has been revealed that “Attention is elsewhere now. I don’t know if it’s complacency or a lack of anxiety, but [the war] is still a pretty big deal,” said oil forecaster Dan Pickering, founder of the Pickering Energy Partners consulting and research firm.

According to recent reports, “What I worry is if the Iranians feel they have to make people anxious again. Do they view it in their strategic interest to create more anxiety?” Pickering noted to Fortune. “I think we’ll have this uneasy conflict going on with Iran for a bunch of 2027.”.

In a recent development, between alternative pipelines and routes, and U.S. escorts through Hormuz, Middle Eastern oil exports are approaching 90% of their prewar levels despite the ongoing military strikes, noted Pavel Molchanov, Raymond James energy analyst. “This indicates that the oil market has become acclimated to periodic flare-ups, just as long as there is no return to all-out war,” he added. “That said, the lack of a U.S.-Iran deal still translates into a hefty risk premium.”.

It has been revealed that because of seasonal demand dips, rising Middle Eastern exports, and President Donald Trump’s emphasis on de-escalating the war since the midterm congressional elections, global oil prices have fallen below the $100 per barrel threshold, even though the global benchmark remains high at more than $90. After all, the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is dangerously depleted at a 44-year low, and the world has cumulatively lost 2.8 billion barrels of oil over nearly nine months, the IEA report stated.

According to recent reports, the Iran war has triggered record-high fuel spikes in the U.S. But keep in mind that the U.S. leads the world in oil output, presently producing an all-time high of more than 14 million barrels daily. The rest of the world is left even more at the mercy of the war, and the price spikes and physical shortages are amplified, especially in Asia and Africa.

More than 4 billion people—roughly half the global population—depended on the Middle East for over 30% of its oil supplies. And about 80% of Middle Eastern oil exports were destined for Asia before the war.

Even as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Iraq move to build pipelines to divert oil supplies through alternate routes, those projects will take years, and long-term Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz would maintain uncertainty going forward.

“That’s not a particularly comforting outlook to the consumers of Middle East crude,” Pickering said. “The finish matters, and I don’t think we have visibility on what the finish looks like.”.

The Americas are leading the increase in oil production—the U.S., Canada, Argentina, Brazil, Guyana, and now Venezuela—as well as a slate of African nations. And more countries are investing in renewable energy and electrification for electric vehicles.

Birol and the IEA forecast that renewables—solar, wind, and batteries—are picking up momentum throughout the world even as the globe falls short of its climate change goals. Nuclear power also is gaining steam. EV sales are projected to rise in most of the world next year—less so in the U.S.—in part because of cheaper, subsidized Chinese EVs being exported worldwide.

Global oil demand is now expected to peak by 2030 and slowly decline from there, the IEA mentioned. Natural gas demand will grow through the mid-2030s and plateau.

The IEA outlook noted that August was the hottest month ever on record worldwide and a strong El Niño could add to weather-related strains heading into 2027. “High energy prices and shortfalls in fertilizer supply are creating hazards for food security,” the report stated. “Emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) and air pollutants from fuel combustion remain dangerously high. Energy geopolitics are fracturing, and trade restrictions are on the rise. Trust is in short supply. Each vulnerability deepens the others.”.

That is why—more than ever—the world requires “credible road maps to phase out fossil fuels, backed by the public finance needed to ensure a fast and fair transition,” said David Tong, global industry lead at Oil Change International.

“Fossil fuels are driving chaos and high energy bills, and the energy choices we make now will shape all our futures,” Tong added. “After yet another fossil fuel crisis, governments cannot afford to keep people and economies hooked on volatile oil and gas markets.”.
